Position Summary

The Senior Facilities Technician is responsible for the operation, maintenance, repair, and reliability of building systems supporting regulated laboratory, warehouse, and office environments across multiple locations. This position performs preventive and corrective maintenance, troubleshooting, inspections, repairs, and environmental monitoring to ensure facilities operate safely, efficiently, and in compliance with applicable requirements.
The role serves as a technical resource for the Facilities team and works closely with internal stakeholders, Property Management, contractors, and vendors to support reliable facility operations and business needs.

Job Responsibilities

  • Operate, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair facility systems and equipment, including HVAC, BMS/BAS controls, plumbing, electrical, lighting, security, pumps, motors, valves, and other mechanical systems.

  • Maintain appropriate environmental conditions within regulated laboratories, warehouse/operations areas, and general office spaces.

  • Perform and document preventive maintenance (PM), corrective maintenance (CM), inspections, troubleshooting, and repairs in accordance with established procedures and safety requirements.

  • Monitor BMS/BAS systems, respond to alarms, troubleshoot equipment and control issues, and support reliable operation of environmental control systems.

  • Document maintenance, repairs, inspections, and other assigned work accurately and timely within the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).

  • Identify recurring equipment issues and recommend improvements to preventive maintenance programs and facility reliability.

  • Perform general building maintenance, including minor plumbing, carpentry, drywall repair, painting, furniture moves, shelving installation, and office modifications.

  • Coordinate staff moves and workspace reconfigurations as needed.

  • Coordinate and oversee contractors, vendors, janitorial services, and Property
    Management activities; verify work completion, service documentation, and invoices.

  • Support facility safety and compliance inspections, including testing assigned safety equipment and maintaining required inspection logs.

  • Provide technical guidance and mentoring to Facilities technicians as needed.

  • Partner with laboratory leadership, Quality, and other stakeholders to support facility requirements and business operations.

  • Follow applicable OSHA, environmental, health, safety, and hazardous material handling requirements and maintain a clean and safe work environment.

  • Travel between assigned locations and provide after-hours/on-call support for facility and environmental control system emergencies.

  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned.

Required Qualifications

  • High School diploma or GED

  • Valid driver's license.

  • Five (5) or more years of related facilities maintenance experience, preferably supporting regulated or critical environments.

  • Three (3) or more years of experience operating and troubleshooting Building Management Systems (BMS/BAS) and related controls.

  • EPA CFC Universal Certification.

  • Hands-on experience with HVAC and working knowledge of electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and general building systems.

  • Experience performing and documenting preventive and corrective maintenance within a CMMS.

  • Strong troubleshooting, problem-solving, communication, and organizational skills.

  • Ability to coordinate contractors and vendors and work effectively with internal stakeholders.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting cleanrooms, laboratories, life sciences, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, healthcare, or other critical environments.

  • Ability to read and interpret mechanical, electrical, and plumbing (MEP) drawings and blueprints.

  • Knowledge of building automation, HVAC controls, environmental monitoring, and preventive maintenance programs.

  • Experience providing technical guidance or mentoring to other Facilities technicians.

Physical Demands

  • Must possess ability to sit, stand, and/or work at a computer for long periods of time.

  • Ability to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

  • May be exposed to extreme temperatures, elevated noise levels, fumes, blood-borne pathogens, biohazardous materials, and chemicals, including formalin, within laboratory environments.

  • Must be able to safely work in mechanical, laboratory, warehouse, and office environments.

Training

  • All job specific, safety, and compliance training are assigned based on the job functions associated with this employee.

Other

  • This position requires periodic travel between work locations and may require a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays. Participation in an on-call rotation and after-hours response to facility, HVAC, and environmental control system emergencies may be required.

Conditions of Employment: Individual must successfully complete pre-employment process, which includes criminal background check, drug screening, credit check ( applicable for certain positions) and reference verification.

Position Summary:

  • This position collects data in the feed conversion houses and dissection laboratory by using measuring instruments and electronic devices. Other duties may be assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Basic computer skills for inputting data regarding dissection data via tablet.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Collect Data and Perform House Checklist within Feed Conversion Houses and Brood Feed Conversion Houses performing the following duties: weigh chickens into and out of their cages; record and add feed to feeders as needed; collect data with pen and paper and/or on a computer or tablet; check bird’s heart rate and blood oxygen with pulse-oximeter following the accepted protocols; dispose of dead birds as instructed; feed birds according to schedules; clean and disinfect equipment; house set-up; perform routine housekeeping duties; segregate birds according to line and sex as instructed; remove and place birds in cages according to schedules; examine birds for signs of illness and report any problems to lead or manager; monitor controls and thermostats that regulate temperature and humidity of the poultry house; perform simple math as part of recording information according to instructions such as bird weight, feed, added feed, and mortality; repair, align, and construct cages, pens or equipment (feeders, water lines, lights, vents, etc) (50%)

  • Collect Data within Dissection Laboratory performing the following duties: euthanize birds; use scalpel to dissect birds into

specific parts to accepted protocols; visually score for defects in physiology; use a caliper to collect data; enter weights and defects into tablet or computer; dispose of dead dissect birds into incinerators (40%)

Other duties, responsibilities, and activities:

  • These may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice, such as: collect swab samples; clean, disinfect, and haul coops; maintain foot bath, hand sanitizer, hydro-foamer, sweep, mop, and other general cleaning; properly euthanize weak/ill birds in accordance with company policy (10%)

Biosecurity/Animal Welfare:

  • The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear is provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

The successful candidate(s) must be willing and able to perform the physical requirements of the job with or without reasonable accommodation.

  • Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly lift and/or move 25 pounds , and occasionally up to 50 pounds, items such as cases of Synergize, supplies, etc; required to occasionally use wheeled dollies to lift and/or move up to 500 pounds of feed, supplies, etc. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift on concrete; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects and controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; climbing/ladder usage; stoop/bend up to 1000 times per day; repetitive hand/wrist movements while dissecting birds with scalpel, knife or other cutting instrument; talk or hear; drive a vehicle within the farm complex. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus. Must have good communication skills to accurately convey opinions and concerns.

  • Tools and Equipment: Scale, Tablet, Scanner, Scalpel, Drill, Safety Knife, Pressure Washer

  • Environment: Required to work on wet, slippery surfaces and also work in hot, dry, extreme dusty, wet and cold environments.

  • Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles, safety glasses, face shield, chemical gloves, cutting gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required. Ear plugs will be used as needed. NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators will be worn as needed.

  • Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants such as Synergize, Virocid, Simple Green, Lysol, etc.

  • Safety: TM is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. TM is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks.

title: Studio Experience Team- Bucktown
description:
OUR PEOPLE POWER OUR PURPOSE

The CorePower team is the heartbeat of the company. We prioritize our people first, and we are invested the employee experience so that together we can create an experience powerful enough to transform lives, including our own. We believe in the power of human connection, community, and going beyond the transactional to make a positive difference in people’s lives. Join our team and discover what happens when you ignite your intention to make a difference.

HOW WE SHOW UP

We are fiercely committed to our core values of empowering everyone, practicing gratitude, building community, growing forward and laughing together. These core values align us in service of CorePower’s higher purpose – to power love from the inside out. They are our guiding principles; internal agreements we make as a CorePower team about how we interact with each other and our students. Living our core values means they guide all our activities, define our workplace culture, and ensure there are no missed opportunities to fulfill our higher purpose.

We embrace our differences and foster an inclusive space where everyone can reach their full potential. We uplift, inspire and guide one another. We make time to share the power of yoga together, celebrate milestones and find joy in the present moment.

ROLE SUMMARY

In doing our part to make yoga more accessible to all, we have created a role that will allow us to positively impact the student experience at each of our studios and provide a discount on our studio membership. A CorePower Yoga (CPY) Studio Experience Team (SET) member is an important role to our overall student experience. We are seeking a reliable and detail-oriented individual to join our team as a SET member. The ideal candidate will be responsible for maintaining a clean and hygienic environment for our yoga studio, ensuring that it is always ready for use by our community.

As a SET member you can deepen your connection with the CPY community and strengthen your personal yoga practice by taking advantage of a special discounted yoga membership (prices and max hours vary by market). Additionally, our SET members exhibit the Company’s Core Values of Empower Everyone, Practice Gratitude, Build Community, Grow Forward, & Laugh Together.

If you are passionate about cleanliness and take pride in creating a welcoming and serene environment, we would love to hear from you. This is a part-time position in which our SET members commit to up to six hours of studio shifts per month.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES

  • Clean and disinfect all areas of the yoga studio, including floors, walls, mirrors, windows, and surfaces.

  • Maintain the cleanliness of the reception area, changing rooms, and bathrooms.

  • Ensure that yoga props and equipment, such as mats, blocks, and straps, are clean and organized.

  • Restock supplies, such as paper towels, toilet paper, and soap.

  • Take out the trash and recycling ensuring that all waste is properly disposed of.

  • Assist with laundry, including folding towels and other linens.

  • Notify management of any maintenance or repair needs in the studio.

  • Must be able to commit to a schedule and follow the CPY Time and Attendance Policy.

SKILLS & QUALIFICATIONS

  • Ability to commit to 6 hours per month (schedule varies based on studio need).

  • Ability to work independently and efficiently.

  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills.

  • Knowledge of proper cleaning techniques and disinfectants.

  • Ability to lift and move heavy equipment, such as yoga mats and props.

  • Availability to work early mornings, evenings, and weekends.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Prior cleaning or housekeeping experience is preferred.

  • Must adhere to CPY’s attendance policy.

SET DISCOUNTED ALL ACCESS MEMBERSHIP

You are eligible to purchase a Studio Experience Team Discounted All Access Membership, which is an exclusive membership option available only to the SET team. It includes:

  • Retail discounts

  • Buddy Pass access

  • Discounts on CPY teacher trainings (200-Hour Yoga Teacher Certification + 50-Hour Yoga Sculpt/CorePower Strength X Teacher Certifications)

COMPENSATION

  • 17.05 per hour

THE PERKS

  • Discounted All Access Membership - use anytime, in studio or online

  • Retail Discounts

  • Continued Education Offerings

  • Access to Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

  • 1.5x Holiday Pay: Earn time-and-a-half pay for hours worked on New Year’s Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day.

WHO WE ARE

At CorePower Yoga, we live our power by showing the world the incredible life-changing things that happen when you root an intensely physical workout in the mindfulness of yoga. This is our promise. We are the nation’s largest yoga studio brand with over 200 locations across the country, digital livestream and on-demand classes, and thousands of passionate yoga teachers sharing the transformative power of our practice.

As a team, we love seeing the magic that happens in a CorePower Yoga class when physical meets mindful and strive to create a work environment that mirrors the balance, empowerment and community experienced in our yoga studios.

title: OPERATING DEPARTMENTAL PRACTITIONER , OPERATION THEATRE
description:
GENERAL DESCRIPTION
Accountable for providing professional nursing care in surgery, anesthesia, recovery, and central sterilizing supply services, to patients within a hospital unit, adhering to hospital policies and nursing services principles, policies, and procedures to ensure high quality care is practiced.

JOB DESCRIPTION
ORGANIZATION AND MANAGEMENT

IN THE OPERATION THEATRE:

  • Adherence to nursing care vision, mission, goals, and objectives, aligns with the scope of nursing services, and performs duties as assigned by the Unit Manager to ensure high-quality care is rendered.
  • Notifies the unit manager of any changes in the situation that could impact the standards of care.
  • Provide the operation theatre room ready for use by checking the completion of damp dusting, checking the gas cylinders, testing all equipment in good order, replenishing stocks like lotion, suture, and procedure set, and preparing trolleys for use.
  • Collaborate with ward staff to ensure patients arrive on time for procedures, optimizing OT utilization.
  • Participates in the unit meetings, dialogue sessions, and other hospital activities.
  • Collaborate with the unit manager in maintaining accurate records of linen, equipment, and medical supplies, condemning old or unusable items for disposal if necessary, carrying out assigned tasks, and providing feedback
  • Charge accurately, incorporating charges for equipment and consumable items into the patient's charges and verifying their completeness.
  • Inspect, maintain, and document the supply of sterile packs to ensure the integrity of the packaging and maintain an adequate supply of unit stock from central sterile supply services.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

A SCRUB AND RECOVERY STAFF:

  • Verify patient identity and surgery details according to the OT list in the reception area and accompany patients safely into the operating rooms.
  • Provide necessary surgical instruments, arranging them according to usage, maintaining sterility, and ensuring an adequate supply of lotions and items according to the surgeon's preference.
  • Performing a surgical hand scrub, wearing a sterile gown and gloves, and preparing and positioning the patient according to the type of surgery.Anticipating surgeon needs, assisting in coagulation of bleeders, maintaining instrument sterility and cleanliness, passing correct specimens to the circulating nurse, performing swab and instrument counts, and notifying if there is any fault.
  • Support surgeons in all operative procedures, consultants about the care of patients in the Operation Theatre, resuscitation of patients in emergency, and report counts as correct or incorrect to the surgeon.
  • Check, and handle the specimens properly after each case, confirming with the registered nurse or surgeon, if necessary, before sending them to the laboratory or pathology services
  • Provide cleanliness and organize the drapes and instruments, responsible disposal of sharps in designated containers, and complete all case-related documents
  • Accompany patients safely into the recovery room before being sent to the ward and record all cases in the Operation Theatre Record Book.
  • Collaborate with registered nurses to provide high-quality care, performing specific post-operative instructions as ordered, ensuring patient safety, monitoring vital signs, managing surgical drainage systems, collecting specimens and laboratory results, completing documentation, and notifying abnormal findings


​AN ANAESTHESIA STAFF:

  • Provide patient education and reassurance before surgery, avoid unnecessary conversation if the patient is drowsy because of the pre-medication, and assess patients' medical history and allergies.
  • Prepare a wide range of specialist equipment and drugs, including anesthetic machines, intravenous equipment, and airway devices.
  • Provide patient safety during anesthesia such as checking for denture removal, loose teeth, and contact lens removal, and ask to confirm any oral intake.



JOB REQUIREMENT ​

  • Certificate in Operating Department Practice Program or Diploma in Operating Department Practice Program

Knowledge and Experiences:

  • Certified Basic Life Support would be a priority.

  • Experience working in a hospital is an advantage.

  • Experience assisting the surgeon in various disciplines of surgery.

Special skills required

  • Able to converse fluently and write in English and Bahasa Malaysia

  • Microsoft Office literacy.

title: Engineering Lead
description:
We’re looking for people to join the Access family, who share our passion for believing in better, and who will help us continue to grow.

Love Work. Love Life. Be You. - is central to our success and how we give our customers the freedom to do more of what's important to them.

What does Access offer you?

We offer a blended approach to office working, encouraging you to collaborate and connect in one of our thriving offices. We deliver on what we say, taking the development of our people seriously. We’ll work with you to progress your success plan and provide opportunities to accelerate your career.

Position Summary

The Lead Software Engineer is a ‘50:50’ role. Half the time you are in the code — shipping production software, holding the technical bar and setting the standard the team follows. The other half you are leading the people, the process and the architecture — running a high-performing engineering stream and developing the engineers within it.

You’ll be joining a small, value-aligned structure: up to two streams of four engineers each, with Product cover per stream. QA is owned by engineering — there is no handoff to a separate team, and that is by design.

The F&B Software Company sits within Access Hospitality, with engineering teams distributed globally, and powers many millions of guest experiences every day. The portfolio includes ResDiary, Dish Cult, DesignMyNight, Collins, Tonic, Soda, Wireless Social, Paytronix, Paytronix Online Ordering, QikServe Digital Ordering, Kiosk, QikServe Connect, Access EPOS, Newbridge POS, GuestPOS, Acteol, Trail, Maintain, RotaReady and CPL.

AI augmentation is a pre-requisite for this role, not an optional extra. Access has invested in cutting-edge AI tooling and we expect every engineer and leader to use AI pervasively to accelerate outcomes, raise quality, and shorten feedback loops. Lead Software Engineers are expected to model this behaviour, embed it into team standards and hold the bar for AI adoption across their streams. If you are not already working this way, you will need to get there fast.

Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities

Technical Leadership

  • Spend approximately half your time as a hands-on engineer: writing, reviewing and shipping production code to the same standard you hold your team to.
  • Own the technical direction of your stream — architecture decisions, technology choices, design patterns and code standards.
  • Set and maintain the engineering quality bar: code review standards, test coverage expectations, CI/CD discipline, observability and security practice.
  • Identify and address technical debt proactively, balancing pragmatism with the long-term health of the codebase.
  • Contribute to platform-wide architectural decisions, feeding your stream’s experience and evidence back into broader engineering strategy.

People Leadership

  • Own the performance, development and wellbeing of up to eight engineers across your streams.
  • Run regular 1:1s, set clear goals, and give direct, actionable feedback — both positive and developmental.
  • Manage the full performance cycle for your engineers: goal setting, mid-year reviews, end-of-year assessments and, where necessary, performance improvement plans.
  • Identify growth opportunities for each engineer and actively create the conditions for them to progress.
  • Hire well — contribute to recruitment, assess candidates rigorously, and take accountability for the quality of who joins your team.
  • Model the behaviours and working practices you expect from the team, including AI adoption, communication standards and engineering discipline.

Delivery & Process

  • Keep your streams delivering consistently — predictable throughput, low change failure rate, fast recovery when things go wrong.
  • Own the engineering process within your streams: sprint ceremonies, planning quality, backlog health and cross-team dependency management.
  • Work closely with Product to balance feature delivery against technical investment, making the trade-offs visible and explicit rather than absorbed silently.
  • Remove blockers for your engineers — escalate where needed, resolve where you can, and protect the team’s ability to focus.
  • Ensure incidents are handled well: fast triage, clear communication, thorough post-mortems, and unique failures — the same class of incident should not recur.

Key Performance Indicators

Technical

  • Software owned by your streams meets reliability, latency and availability targets in production.
  • Lead time for change trends downwards; deployment frequency trends upwards across your streams.
  • Change failure rate stays under 15%; MTTR trends downwards.
  • Critical and high security vulnerabilities patched within agreed SLAs (1 day / 14 days).
  • AI tooling is a demonstrable, routine part of your workflow and embedded visibly in team standards.

People

  • Engineers in your streams have clear goals, regular feedback and a development plan they understand.
  • Regrettable attrition is low; engineers in your streams are growing and progressing.
  • Performance issues are identified early and managed directly, without escalation becoming the default.
  • New hires reach productive contribution within an agreed onboarding window.

Delivery

  • Your streams deliver predictably against commitments made to Product and stakeholders.
  • Failures are unique — the same defect or incident class does not recur.
  • Technical debt is visible, prioritised and moving in the right direction.

Skills, Knowledge, Experience & Qualifications

How We Work

Before the tech stack, this is what working in the F&B engineering team looks like. As a Lead Software Engineer you are expected to model these standards, not just meet them.

  • AI tooling is your default starting point, not a fallback — Copilot, Claude Code, Devin, Cursor or equivalent are open before you write the first line.
  • You use AI pervasively across the full development lifecycle: generating and reviewing code, writing tests, producing documentation, triaging incidents and researching unfamiliar domains.
  • You can prompt effectively — you know how to get useful output, iterate on it, and critically evaluate what comes back rather than accepting it at face value.
  • You treat AI-generated code with the same scrutiny as code from a colleague — it gets reviewed, tested and owned by you.
  • You actively embed AI working practices into your team — through standards, playbooks, code review culture and leading by example.
  • You improve your AI working practices continuously and bring the team with you; this field moves fast and standing still is falling behind.
  • Expect your interview process to include assessment on how you work with AI tooling — not just what you know without it. Come prepared to demonstrate your workflow, not just talk about it.

Technical Foundation

The fundamentals are non-negotiable — your technical credibility is what earns the trust of your engineers.

  • Strong commercial software engineering background with a track record of shipping production systems end-to-end.
  • Clean code, automated testing and CI/CD discipline — you set the standard, which means you have to embody it.
  • Comfortable across the stack — backend, frontend or full-stack — able to review and contribute across the breadth of what your streams own.
  • Solid SQL and relational database skills; experience with cloud-hosted databases in production.
  • Experience designing and consuming RESTful APIs and/or event-driven architectures.
  • Familiarity with containerisation (Docker, Kubernetes or equivalent).
  • Experience making and communicating architectural decisions, including the trade-offs involved.

Leadership & People

  • Proven experience leading a software engineering team — setting direction, managing performance and developing engineers.
  • Direct, honest and constructive communicator — comfortable giving difficult feedback and having conversations that matter.
  • Able to manage competing priorities across engineering and people responsibilities without dropping either.
  • Experience running engineering process — agile delivery, planning, retrospectives, incident management.
  • Comfortable working asynchronously across distributed teams (UK and India).

Technologies

Access F&B runs a broad and evolving tech stack. We care far more about solid fundamentals and the ability to learn than exact technology match.

  • Java — present across several F&B product areas.
  • TypeScript / React — frontend and web-based ordering and management interfaces.
  • Azure — our primary cloud platform; experience with Azure-native services (App Service, Service Bus, SQL, AKS, Key Vault) is valuable.
  • AWS — also present across parts of the F&B portfolio.

Security & Compliance

  • Working knowledge of security fundamentals: auth and authorisation patterns, secrets management, encryption at rest and in transit, and PII handling.

title: Summer 2027 Mars Snacking Global Design Internship
description:
Job Description:

At Mars, we work together to build a better world for people, pets, and the planet. From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter.

As an Associate, you are empowered with the freedom and tools to be yourself, to forge your own path, to build relationships across our global community, to discover the right opportunities for you to grow – all with ample support. Here, you have our ongoing commitment to your growth and development as you work across our world-famous brands.

Start your journey at Mars today!

Mars Snacking Global Design Internship Experience

As a Global Design Intern, you will gain exposure to the following areas:

  • In this role, you will be an active contributor to both brand design and front-end innovation work. You will support the development of product packaging graphics, help visualize new product and portfolio concepts, contribute to innovation strategy frameworks, and assist in the facilitation of creative workshops. This is a unique opportunity to learn how real-world design systems function across global brands while building your professional skills through concept development, storytelling, presentations, and hands-on use of both AI-powered and traditional design tools.

  • Support the development of packaging & branding across some of the world’s most iconic snacking brands, from early concepts through production-ready design.

  • Contribute to front-end innovation projects by helping visualize new product concepts, portfolio opportunities, and brand experiences.

  • Participate in workshops that bring together cross-functional partners to solve business and design challenges.

  • Create presentations, mood boards, concept boards, and visual storytelling materials that communicate ideas clearly to stakeholders.

  • Explore and apply emerging AI-powered creative tools alongside industry-standard design workflows to accelerate ideation and creative development.

  • Collaborate with marketers, R&D, packaging engineers, consumer insights, and other cross-functional partners throughout the product development process.

  • Develop an understanding of global brand systems, packaging design, innovation strategy, and consumer-centered design thinking.

What we’re looking for:

  • Desired majors: Industrial Design, Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or related design disciplines.

  • A portfolio demonstrating strong creative thinking, design fundamentals, and visual communication skills is required.

  • Proficiency with macOS, Adobe Creative Cloud (Illustrator, Photoshop, and InDesign), AI-powered creative tools, and Microsoft Office.

  • Experience with sketching, Figma, Blender, motion graphics or other visualization software is a plus, but not required.

  • Strong communication, collaboration, organization, and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects in a fast-paced environment.

  • We are seeking a creative and collaborative student, sophomore year or older, to join our team.

  • Open to students legally authorized to work in the U.S., without the need for current or future work status authorization or visa sponsorship for employment.

  • Employment is contingent upon successful completion of drug & background screening.

What can you expect from Mars?

  • The Mars Internship Experience is a 10-week summer program providing excellent depth of experience with real business problems and opportunities.

  • Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders.

  • Best-in-class training and development from Day 1, including a formal mentor, access to our in-house Mars University, and more.

  • Ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you succeed and get the most out of your experience.

  • Some pretty sweet perks including competitive salary & benefits package, fun freebies, and pet-friendly offices.

  • Eligible candidates will be responsible for personal transportation to and from work site during duration of the internship program.

About Mars, Incorporated

For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. This idea is at the center of who we have always been as a global, family-owned business. Today, Mars is transforming, innovating, and evolving in ways that affirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the world around us.

Across our diverse and expanding portfolio of Snacking, Food, and Petcare products and services, we employ over 140,000 dedicated Associates who are all moving in the same direction: forward. As a $65 billion family-owned business, we produce some of the world’s best-loved brands including ROYAL CANIN®, PEDIGREE®, WHISKAS®, CESAR®, M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, Pringles®, Cheez-It®, and BEN’S ORIGINAL™. and take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health and services businesses, including AniCura, Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, and VCA™.

We know we can only be truly successful if our partners and the communities in which we operate prosper as well. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today.

For more information about Mars, please visit . Join us on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube.

title: Sr Data Scientist (remote)
description:
We’re excited about your interest in pursuing the next step in your career with US Foods! Your continuous growth and development is critical to our success.

US Foods is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodation to individuals with disabilities. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the interview process or to perform essential job functions, please contact our US Foods Application Accommodation Line at 855-873-2468. You will be prompted to leave a message. Please state the specifics of the assistance needed and your contact information. A member of our HR department will return your call within two business days.

NOTE: Before you begin your internal job search, please review the criteria you will need to start the process.

The Sr Data Scientist executes statistical and mathematical analyses to support business decision-making. This role supports artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) in a deployed production environment. They are experts in the field of Data Science. Consequently, the Sr Data Scientist proactively works with cross-functional teams to seek and understand the business/domain context of potential problems that may be solved using ML. They present data science solutions to stakeholders in an iterative fashion. The Sr. Data Scientist works with Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists in converting a business problem into an ML problem and kickstarting foundational work including data exploration, feature engineering, basic hypothesis testing, and creation of baseline models. They create the model feasibility document in close collaboration with the Data Scientists and Sr Data Scientists. The Sr Data Scientist may have direct reports including Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists.

The work for the Sr Data Scientist position is completely remote anywhere in the United States except Hawaii or United States Territories.

RESPONSIBILITIES

As a Sr Data Scientist, you will be expected to:

  • Work with Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists in researching data sources, data cleansing, feature engineering, and creating baseline models

  • Independently manage multiple data science model development/projects

  • Collaborate and engage with various cross-functional stakeholders to ensure close coordination between data science and business stakeholders including the product management team

  • Provide full ownership of the model development from inception to implementation including the machine learning pipeline, documentation, model drift, and remodeling strategy

  • Mentor the Associate Data Scientists and Data Scientists in data science knowledge and their interactions with other stakeholders

  • Coordinate with the ML team, anticipating deployment issues upfront, setting the stage for resource requirements, and ensuring the success of model deployment and retraining

  • Take and delegate ownership of critical tickets or issues faced by business stakeholders as assigned by the Lead Data Scientist or Director of Data Science

  • Read and independently navigate through extensive codebase with a focus on troubleshooting, debugging, and/or improvement of code

  • Contribute to coding standards and coding conventions and proactively participate in enforcing sound coding practices across the data science team

  • Create and maintain documentation of the ML models, data sources, and methodology

  • Assist in the creation of feasibility documents

  • Proactively participate in the core team processes including R&D, recommending, and implementing process improvements or new methodologies

  • Share knowledge with other various teams and members by presentation at periodic internal team sessions/workshops

  • Guide usage of development methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, etc.) and assist in their implementation in the group projects by deciphering details including features, tasks, estimates of efforts and timing, etc.

SUPERVISION:

  • N/A

RELATIONSHIPS

  • Internal: Associate Data Scientists, Data Scientists, Lead Data Scientists, Principal Data Scientists, and Director of DS.

WORK ENVIRONMENT

  • Remote

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

As a Sr. Data Scientist, you have:

  • Master’s degree in data science/mathematics/CS/statistics or similar field and 3+ years of experience OR Bachelor's degree and 6+ years of experience in data science

  • Effective written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work and communicate effectively with team members and cross-functional teams

  • An expert-level understanding of the following topics:

    • Classification, Regression, Clustering, Dimensionality reduction, Association rule learning, Bagging (e.g., Random Forests), Boosting (e.g., AdaBoost, Gradient Boosting), Neural Networks and Deep Learning, Model Evaluation and Metrics, Cross-validation, Hyperparameter Tuning, Optimization Algorithms, NLP and more

  • Working knowledge of Agile/SCRUM methodologies with 1-2 years of experience and a practical understanding of the epics, features, and tasks that may be most relevant and how much effort is required for them

  • Sufficient intellectual curiosity to investigate the latest developments in the field (for example LLM/Generative AI models)

  • Ability to see the big picture and anticipate issues in terms of deployment limitations, data latency, appropriateness of a particular implementation of algorithms, and mathematical details/assumptions

  • At least 1+ years of working with a major cloud platform, creating ML models using frameworks from data exploration to deployment

  • Working knowledge in handling large datasets in a cloud environment

  • Working knowledge of how APIs work, CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment)

  • Understanding of DevOps and MLOps principles

  • 1+ years of writing production-grade code in scripting languages including Bash, Python, and SQL with the ability to identify the areas of improvement, optimal choice of data structures, optimization of the code, and creating custom code to address unique situations

  • Proven, independent ability to navigate a data lake environment while creating training datasets or feature stores

  • Effective skills in creating, deploying, and troubleshooting containers in the context of ML modeling

  • 1+ years of experience with version control systems/concepts, such as Git, for tracking changes in machine learning projects

  • Ability to investigate/research ML frameworks/algorithms, datasets, feature stores, and contribute to solving data science problems

  • Capability of providing macro-level thought leadership to the junior members including the Data Scientists regarding best practices, issues, causes, and respective resolutions of those issues

This role may also receive annual incentive plan bonus. ​

​Benefits for this role may include health insurance, pre-tax spending accounts, retirement benefits, paid time off, short-term and long-term disability, employee stock purchase plan, and life insurance. description:

By joining the American Red Cross you will touch millions of lives every year and experience the greatness of the human spirit at its best. Are you ready to be part of the world's largest humanitarian network?

Join us—Where your Career is a Force for Good!

Job Description:

Executive Director, Orange County, CA

This position involves very little operational responsibility. It is an external-facing, community relations and fundraising position. It is a plus if the successful candidate has established connections within the community.

WHY CHOOSE US?
Joining the American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional, yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. You grow your career within a movement that matters, where success is measured in people helped, communities made whole, and individuals equipped to never stop changing lives and situations for the better.

When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.

Where Your Career is a Force for Good!

We are currently seeking a professional, innovative and enthusiastic Executive Director for our Orange County Chapter, based in Santa Ana, California.

The American Red Cross of Orange County serves 34 cities and 3.1 million people.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW

The Chapter Executive Director (ED) serves as the primary community facing leader and facilitator for the American Red Cross at the chapter level. As a facilitative meta-leader, the ED, in partnership with functional supervisors, convenes, aligns, and empowers cross-functional teams and external partners to deliver core services, deploy secondary services where needed most, and strengthen community resilience. The ED represents the organization publicly, leads collaborative chapter planning with and alongside the community, and stewards strategic relationships to achieve regional program, revenue, volunteer recruitment & engagement, blood collection, and community engagement goals.

The American Red Cross Orange County Chapter is seeking a dynamic, community-centered Executive Director to serve as the face, voice, and catalyst of our mission across one of the nation’s most diverse and vibrant communities.

This is a unique opportunity for a visionary leader who thrives on building relationships, mobilizing resources, and inspiring collective action. As the chapter’s principal external leader, the Executive Director will elevate the Red Cross presence across Orange County—engaging donors, volunteers and community partners to advance humanitarian impact and long-term resilience.

PAY INFORMATION: The salary range for this position is (California) is: $120,780 - $130,281 + an excellent incentive plan. This position is not eligible for relocation.

WHERE YOUR CAREER IS A FORCE GOOD

Community Leadership & Representation

  • Primary community facing leader of the American Red Cross –maximizing presence, connectivity, and recognition of Red Cross contributions in the community.

  • Span organizational boundaries and bridge silos for coordinated community response (“unity of effort”).

  • Ensure upward, downward, and outward connectivity—coordinating stewardship across Programs, Communications, and Fundraising.

Chapter Planning & Regional Framework

  • Participate as a member of the Regional Leadership Team to support achievement of regional program, revenue, volunteer recruitment & engagement, blood collection, and community engagement goals.

  • Lead the chapter planning process and drive progress toward plan objectives. Convene and align cross-functional teams and external stakeholders across sectors (government, nonprofit, business, faith) to co-create chapter plans with shared outcomes, roles, and accountability.

  • Use data and community voice to prioritize where secondary services are deployed to close gaps, strengthen resilience, and improve equity of access to Red Cross services.

Revenue & Fundraising

  • Lead the chapter in supporting the achievement of the region’s revenue targets

  • Meet the assigned individual fundraising target which includes,

    • Meet the annual chapter board members’ give and get campaign goals,

    • Maintain assigned donor accounts as defined by the Regional Executive and CDO.

  • Actively participating in influencing fundraising in conjunction with the Chief Development Officer.

  • In partnership with the CDO, recruit, develop, and support philanthropy committee members who have philanthropic influence in the community and will actively play a leadership role in fundraising.

Strategic Relationships & Elected Officials

  • Manage a portfolio of strategic relationships: local elected officials, key community leaders & stakeholders. Specific outcomes are defined with RE.

  • Serve as a member of the Elected Officials Liaison Network. Support disaster responses locally, regionally, and nationally consistent with ConOps.

Board Governance & Development

  • Develop, support, and ensure the success of the Chapter Board of Directors in support of the Red Cross mission.

  • Manage and ensure the board meets published board guidance for membership.

Volunteer Leadership

  • Develop, lead, and manage a cadre of community volunteer leaders who serve as the face of the Red Cross in assigned territories.

  • Support mission capacity building by developing and stewarding key community partnerships and support recruitment of volunteers.

Team Member Partnerships

  • Serve as a partner team member to Communications and Fundraising teams to align messaging, stewardship, and campaign execution.

This job will be posted for a minimum of five business days and extended if the applicant pool needs to be expanded. This position IS NOT eligible for relocation.

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED

  • Education: Bachelor's degree required.

  • Experience: Minimum 7 years of related experience or equivalent combination of education and related experience required

  • Demonstrated fundraising experience, including donor engagement and revenue generation

  • Management Experience: NA

  • Skills & Abilities: Ability to work on a team.

  • Travel: May travel and participate in meetings and conferences throughout chapter jurisdiction, state, and Red Cross system.

*Combination of candidate’s education and general experience satisfies requirements so long as the total years equate to description’s minimum education and general experience years combined.

Physical requirements are those present in normal office environment conditions. Operational flexibility is required to meet sudden and unpredictable needs. Ability to use a personal computer, applicable software, and office equipment for sustained periods of time. May include sitting for long periods of time, driving a vehicle, and working under challenging conditions.

WHAT WILL GIVE YOU THE COMPETITIVE EDGE:

  • Preferred candidates will bring a strong, demonstrated connection to and understanding of the local community, enabling effective stakeholder engagement and meaningful impact.

  • Familiarity with local networks and existing community relationships is highly valued.

  • Bilingual (Spanish-speaking) is a plus.

BENEFITS FOR YOU:

We take care of you, while you take care of others. As a mission-based organization, we believe our team needs great support to do great work. Our comprehensive benefits help you in balancing home and work. With our resources and perks, you have amazing possibilities at the American Red Cross.

title: Protection and Advocacy Coordinator
description:
With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local - Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITES:


Policy and Strategy Implementation


Strategy development and implementation of child, humanitarian and policy advocacy

  • Coordinate the development and implementation of WV South Sudan’s national advocacy strategy and plans
  • Coordinate and collaborate with different functional, technical, and zonal teams in ensuring WV South Sudan’s advocacy strategic priorities are integrated and reflected in all existing programmes and those that are in the pipeline
  • Develop policy positions in support of ending child hunger and malnutrition, and violence against children, specific to South Sudan, and to contribute to broader WVI campaign and global humanitarian efforts
  • Provide leadership to research, advocacy, and policy briefs.
  • Ensure implementation and adherence to WV’ s Child Protection and Participation and Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) policies
  • Provide National Director and Senior Leadership Team (SLT) with key messages and resources that enable them to build a healthy culture of protection, and inclusion in their respective functions.
  • Co-create, coordinate and monitor the roll-out an integrated child protection, participation and inclusion action plan with Leadership that articulates specific actions the National Director, SLT, and other Managers will take to create and nurture a safeguarding and inclusive culture
  • Support the FO strategy FY26-30 implementation and measurement with a focus on strategic objective 3, “Children protected from violence and exploitation”
  • Support WV South Sudan staff skills in advocacy through the Advocacy Academy
  • Ensure timely planning, implementation and reporting

Child Protection and Participation

Child Protection Integration

  • Ensure child protection standards are integrated into all programmes, projects, and operational processes.
  • Promote compliance with organizational child safeguarding and protection policies, including mandatory reporting procedures.
  • Support risk assessments and mitigation measures to prevent harm to children in programme implementation.

Child Participation

  • Ensure children are meaningfully and safely engaged in programme design, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.
  • Promote age-appropriate and inclusive mechanisms that enable children to express their views and influence decisions affecting them.
  • Strengthen accountability to children through regular feedback and consultation mechanisms.
  • Support child representation at the WV East Africa Child Advisory Group (EACAG)

Capacity Building

  • Ensure staff, volunteers, and partners complete mandatory child safeguarding training.
  • Build the capacity of teams and partners on child participation principles, child protection standards, and safeguarding requirements.

Monitoring and Compliance

  • Monitor compliance with child protection and safeguarding requirements across assigned programmes.
  • Ensure child participation and safeguarding indicators are tracked, documented, and reported.
  • Address identified gaps through corrective action plans.

Partnership and Representation

  • Collaborate with government authorities, UN agencies, NGOs, and community stakeholders to strengthen child protection systems.
  • Represent the organization in relevant child protection and safeguarding coordination forums, as assigned.

Advocacy, Campaigns and External Engagement

Campaigns, national and global moments: Social mobilisation, staff engagement, and documentation

  • Lead the coordination and integration of the campaign agenda, particularly the ENOUGH Campaign and ending violence against children, across WV South Sudan’s technical programmes and operational areas
  • Coordinate, advise, and guide project teams in different zonal offices on campaign activities at national and local levels
  • Closely monitor and track the progress of the campaign outputs, outcomes, and impact at the national and local level
  • Document the campaigns and global moment participation key milestones and lessons learned
  • The Advocacy Strategic Measures report primarily focuses on our contributions to policy change that impacts the children in South Sudan. Hence it is important that we capture the # of policy (new or updated) we’ve contributed to either through direct engagement with power-holders or through coalitions/consortium/cluster.
  • Advocacy messaging used by WV DMT, WV EU, and other offices across the partnership has been set up in the Box, including the messaging on humanitarian situation, Coalition on Conflict and Hunger, EU Deve
  • Partnership building, networking, and collaborations contributing to enhanced child well-being, child voice, and child participation
  • Advocate and influence partnerships and/or coalitions towards the adoption and /or support for the campaign and policy change agenda at national and local level
  • Coordinate implementation of partnership and/or coalition activities relating to the advocacy and campaign-agenda at the national level
  • Support functionality of established child participation structures including the children’s parliament/council
  • Coordinate activities involving the participation of children in the different advocacy engagements at national level
  • Initiate and maintain data base of child advocates that can support advocacy engagements at the different levels including international fora

Evidence-Based Advocacy

· Support the production of advocacy reports with particular emphasis on giving children a voice.

· Ensure national policy guidelines are aligned with regional / global policy, especially on humanitarian/nexus/fragile context issues, standards and assist in contextualizing them within South Sudan’s fragile context.

· Lead Maturity Framework and Advocacy Success Matrix / Advocacy Strategic Measures (ASM) dialogue and provide quarterly updates for the Country Director. Provide technical support for protection mainstreaming and programming and support research and learning on protection issues.

· Provide evidence, messaging and action items to external stakeholders on World Vision’s advocacy positioning and priorities for South Sudan, namely child protection, violence against children, protection of civilians, fragility, and the humanitarian-development-peacebuilding nexus; Support PDQA in preparation of advocacy reports, position papers and concept papers on Child Wellbeing issues that can contribute to policy dialogue, especially humanitarian advocacy within South Sudan.

· Manage all response related advocacy reporting requirements at national office and to GC level.

Technical Support for Strategy and Program Implementation

  • Participate in resource mobilisation through proposal writing to ensure integration of campaign and policy change agenda in different funding opportunities
  • Support the development of fundable concept notes and design of new projects with a focus on ENOUGH campaign and other campaigns and advocacy initiatives
  • Support the development of sectoral/programmatic capacity statements
  • Work with programmes to increase awareness and understanding of issues of poverty and injustice, and advocate publicly on agreed issues to build World Vision’s credible voice among the public and decision-makers
  • Map out successful project designs with campaign and policy advocacy initiatives and keep track of their implementation
  • Lead the development of advocacy and campaign training packages and information, education, and communication (IEC) materials
  • Support sector-related research, case studies, and learnings, ensuring alignment with World Vision’s positions, and advocacy and campaign agendaContribute to the development, implementation, and measurement of strategy
  • Ensure overall technical quality of all Protection (including CP and GBV) programming;
  • Support project start-up and monitoring to ensure protection & gender mainstreaming;
  • Conduct field visits to assess technical quality, make recommendations, and support follow-through;
  • Facilitate trainings directly, or support field teams/consultants to do so;
  • Provide technical support for the recruitment of Protection-related staff
  • Ensure child participation in all relevant programs, including engagement with the SLT

Resource Acquisition and Management

  • Provide technical support to proposal development for protection, safeguarding, gender mainstreaming, and GBV-related projects across all sectors, including budget design, technical design, theory of change etc, to ensure protection and gender are mainstreamed and risks mitigated.
  • Review ongoing and final reporting of projects before external submission;
  • Review, contextualize, and develop training packages, as necessary;
  • Produce materials for safeguarding, Protection & Gender programming;
  • Support program quality and strategy team in developing assessment, monitoring, and evaluation tools to measure safeguarding, protection, CP, and GBV issues, risks, and build staff capacity in the use of tools;
  • Review TORs for external consultants conducting assessments, evaluations, etc.;
  • Provide technical leadership to sector-related research, case studies, and learnings
  • Participate in the capacity assessment and vetting of programming partners.

Monitoring and Reporting

  • Meet minimum quality standards and support improvement, reflection, learning, and innovation
  • Compile and submit quality reports to operations and advocacy team leaders for further consolidation and management decision-making.
  • Lead the completion of the annual Safeguarding, Protection and Inclusion Update Report and use results to develop or contribute to the annual safeguarding action plan.
  • Analyse progress on safeguarding, protection, and inclusion compliance and quality safeguarding implementation, and use lessons to continue good practices, fill gaps, and improve quality implementation.
  • Ensure a central database is maintained to document complaints and feedback received from all channels. Ensure that the database is updated and utilized daily.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in a Legal, management or Child Rights-related field, or field/practical experience working with situations of policy formation, guidance, and implementation.
  • Technical skills: direct programming or management experience in advocacy, External engagement, child protection in emergencies, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), gender-based violence (GBV), GEDSI and safeguarding
  • Experience: 2-3 years’ + experience in advocacy and external engagement, overseeing child protection, PSEA, GBV, GEDSI, and safeguarding work – preferably in a humanitarian context
  • Other: strong relationship building/network capacity, excellent communication skills, spiritual maturity in Christian faith, ability to influence, innovative, and proactive personality.
  • Humanitarian policy and advocacy expertise, with ability to represent INGO across national and international spaces
  • Project planning and proposal writing certification, or comparable professional experience with proven results
  • Team management, capacity building, and mentorship
  • Good understanding of World Vision, its programs, and policies
  • Excellent writing and documentation skills
  • Strong interpersonal, collaboration, networking, and communications skills

By joining the American Red Cross you will touch millions of lives every year and experience the greatness of the human spirit at its best. Are you ready to be part of the world's largest humanitarian network?

Join us—Where your Career is a Force for Good!

Job Description:

Joining The American Red Cross is like nothing else – it’s as much something you feel as something you do. You become a vital part of the world’s largest humanitarian network. Joining a team of welcoming individuals who are exceptional, yet unassuming. Diverse, yet uncompromising in unity. You grow your career within a movement that matters, where success is measured in people helped, communities made whole, and individuals equipped to never stop changing lives and situations for the better.

When you choose to be a force for good, you’ll have mentors who empower your growth along a purposeful career path. You align your life’s work with an ongoing mission that’s bigger than all of us. As you care for others, you’re cared for with competitive compensation and benefits. You join a community that respects who you are away from work as much as what you do while at work.

Where Your Career is a Force for Good!

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (Job Overview):

When you join our team as a Blood Collection Supervisor you will use your leadership, compassion and customer service skills to lead our blood collection team to going above and beyond ensuring that all donors have the best experience possible. Our Supervisors drive for results and serve others with a high level of respect for our staff and the donors we value.

The Red Cross offers paid phlebotomy training with the ability to grow your skills and career within the nation’s top humanitarian organization. To learn more about the Blood Collection team and how we serve the community, watch this short video: rdcrss.org/lifesavingrole

  • Supervise blood collection staff, including training and performance

  • Drive for results and to serve others with a high level of respect for customer service

  • Take the time to personally connect with donors – listen to their stories and help them understand the value of their donation

  • Contribute to a friendly and fun environment. Team up with your co-workers to keep our donors coming back again and again

Standard Schedule:

  • To best meet the needs of our donors and community, staff work a variable schedule which may include early mornings, late nights, weekends, and holidays. Overnight travel may be required in some locations.

  • Schedule is provided two to three weeks in advance

WHAT YOU NEED TO SUCCEED (Minimum Qualifications):

  • Bachelor’s degree OR a combination of education and work experience (four to eight years of work experience in a related field) is required

  • Minimum of three years of supervisory/leadership experience

  • Customer service experience and effective verbal communication skills are required. An ability to effectively discuss procedures and medical issues with patients, families and physicians needed.

  • A current, valid driver's license with a good driving record is required.

  • Physical requirements may include the ability to lift, push or pull heavy weights up and down ramps and stairs, good manual dexterity, the ability to sit or stand for long periods of time and adapt to long, irregular hours and frequent schedule changes are required. Position may require a minimum height of 60 inches to ensure the ability to safely operate Red Cross vehicles.

  • At the American Red Cross, we conduct many mobile blood drives at businesses, schools and many other locations. All staff work as a team to setup and tear down the equipment required to conduct a mobile blood drive.

  • Basic computer skills are desirable

WHAT WILL GIVE YOU THE COMPETITIVE EDGE (Preferred Qualifications):

  • Prior healthcare or phlebotomy experience (CNA, MA, EMT, etc.)

  • Prior leadership experience exceeding 3 years in a healthcare setting


BENEFITS FOR YOU:

As a mission-based organization, we believe our team needs great support to do great work. Our comprehensive package includes:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision plans

  • Health Spending Accounts & Flexible Spending Accounts

  • PTO: Starting 15 days a year; based on type of job and tenure

  • Holidays: 11 paid holidays comprised of six core holidays and five floating holidays

  • Paid Family Leave

make your career a force for good!

We are seeking qualified applicants for the position:

Advisor II, CSU

Located:

CP2

title: Operational Excellence Change Agent
description:
Be a part of our mission! As a world leader in creating comfortable, sustainable, and efficient climate solutions for buildings, homes and transportation, it's our responsibility to put the planet first. For us at Trane Technologies, and through our businesses including Trane® and Thermo King, sustainability is not just how we do business—it is our business. Do you dare to look at the world's challenges and see impactful possibilities? Do you want to contribute to making a better future? If the answer is yes, we invite you to consider joining us in boldly challenging what's possible for a sustainable world.

Learn about our benefits designed for you to Thrive at work and at home.

We boldly go.

Where is the work:

On-Site (5 days)

What's in it for you:

Trane Technologies is seeking a Continuous Improvement/ Sr. Change Agent in Atlanta, GA to lead and accelerate Lean transformation across site operations. This role is instrumental in driving a culture of continuous improvement by embedding Lean principles, disciplines, and tools into daily business practices. The ideal candidate will be a strategic change leader who can influence all levels of the organization, develop team capability, and deliver measurable gains in safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.

What you will do:

  • Conduct comprehensive value stream analyses to assess current operational and transactional performance, identify process inefficiencies, and define future-state improvements that enhance flow, effectiveness, customer value, and overall business results.
  • Review existing and proposed procedures, workflows, controls, and supporting systems to identify barriers to performance, uncover improvement opportunities, and develop actionable plans that support effective implementation and sustainment of change.
  • Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of Lean improvement activities, including Kaizen events, Blitz events, Rapid Improvement Events (RIEs), and Just Do It (JDI) activities, ensuring strong participation, effective facilitation, and alignment to safety, quality, delivery, cost, and productivity objectives.
  • Train, coach, and support Team Leaders, Supervisors, Managers, and cross-functional teams through daily engagement, team meetings, and Gemba walks, reinforcing effective problem solving and the practical application of Lean tools, principles, and methodologies.
  • Coach and support the use of daily management practices, including Mission Control, MDI, A3 problem solving, standard work, visual controls, and area control boards, to improve accountability, highlight normal versus abnormal conditions, and strengthen team performance.
  • Create, implement, improve, and sustain standard work, visual work aids, and other workplace controls that promote consistency, clarity, and adherence to desired processes.
  • Apply Lean diagnostic and analytical tools such as value stream mapping, cycle time analysis, time studies, line balancing, workplace analysis, and error-proofing methods to identify waste, improve flow, and optimize operational performance.
  • Support leaders and teams in resolving issues that arise during and after Lean improvement events, helping ensure actions are completed, barriers are removed, and desired future-state outcomes are achieved and sustained.
  • Monitor, track, and communicate key improvement metrics and results through visual management systems, control boards, and other reporting methods to confirm effectiveness, sustain gains, and support informed decision-making.
  • Partner closely with the Sr. Value Stream Coach, Site Leader, Department Managers, Supervisors, and cross-functional stakeholders to address challenges during implementation and sustainment phases, ensuring improvement initiatives remain aligned with operational and business objectives.
  • Support the ongoing Lean transformation by identifying training needs, reinforcing management practices, promoting employee engagement, and helping build a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence.
  • Serve as a backup to the Sr. Value Stream Coach when needed, providing leadership continuity and ongoing support for site-wide continuous improvement efforts.

What you will bring:

  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in Lean manufacturing, operational excellence, or continuous improvement, with demonstrated success in managing, training, coaching, and developing others in Lean tools, principles, and methodologies; or equivalent operations leadership experience applying Lean principles and methodologies.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and practical application of Lean manufacturing concepts, continuous improvement tools, and problem-solving methodologies, including value stream mapping, standard work, visual management, waste elimination, and structured event facilitation.
  • Demonstrated success leading and facilitating Kaizen, Blitz, Rapid Improvement Events (RIEs), or similar structured improvement activities, with a strong track record of delivering measurable operational and financial results.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with employees at all levels, from frontline team members to senior leadership, and to facilitate productive group discussions and training sessions.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify issues, collect and interpret data, evaluate process performance, and support practical, sustainable solutions.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Visio, or similar business and process-mapping tools.
  • Experience applying Lean or continuous improvement principles in transactional or administrative processes is preferred.
  • Associate or bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering, mechanical engineering, manufacturing engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent education, training, and relevant work experience will be considered in lieu of a formal degree.

title: Director, TBM Strategy & Planning
description:

As a trusted partner to AVP’s and Sr Directors in the IT division, the Director leads data-driven analysis and contributes recommendations for long-term operating expense and delivery model optimization. Position Summary:

  • This position is responsible for the daily care of flocks in growing houses by performing all essential duties. Other duties may be assigned.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Prepare houses for bird placement by installing metal & wire partitions to form accurate sized pens for bird placement as instructed, setup feed system, and safely operate truck/trailer to transfer birds from FCR to Growout and place in assigned pens (15%)
  • Provide daily care of flock by properly calculating and recording feed amounts using calculator to determine # of pounds per pen, using hopper scale to weigh proper # of pounds per pen, distributing feed into feed hoppers by carrying buckets, monitoring flock for signs of injury/illness/slow growth and placing in recovery pen or euthanizing according to animal welfare policy, and collecting, recording wing band, and disposing of flock mortality, and administer and record medications via the water system as directed by management (30%)
  • Maintains flock environment by flushing water lines weekly by turning flush valve, maintaining pen bedding to animal welfare standards, using handheld electric blower to clear dust from equipment (fans, inlets, etc.) once a week, and verifying feed/water/environmental control systems working properly and report any issues for correction (15%)
  • Collect data regarding bird growth and development by analyzing fleshing (breast size) and sorting as needed, using digital scales to obtain average weight of each pen by weighing 60 females/30 males weekly, collecting weekly lab samples by using boot swabs for environment and cleft pallet swabs for birds, and assisting with euthanasia of birds designated by FCR out list as instructed by manager (30%)

Other duties, responsibilities, and activities:

  • Other duties, responsibilities and activities may change or be assigned at any time with or without notice. Such as: maintain vehicle by checking fluid levels, filters, tire pressure, and clean/disinfect to remove debris, operate a high pressure and regular water hose, maintains foot pans and hand sanitizer, maintains a clean and organized work/break area. (10%)

Biosecurity/Animal Welfare Requirements:

  • The jobsite is a biosecure environment which requires showering, changing clothing and footwear before entering the facility. Appropriate clothing and footwear are provided by the Company. No jewelry may be worn on the jobsite except for medical ID jewelry and body piercings covered by appropriate clothing. Must be willing to sign an agreement to avoid any avian species (chickens, ducks, birds, etc.). Must be willing to sign and abide by the Company Biosecurity and Company Animal Welfare Guidelines.

Physical Demands and Work Environment:

  • Physical: Must use safe lifting techniques. Must regularly lift and carry feed weighing up to 30 pounds and will occasionally be required to lift and carry bundles of shavings weighing up to 12 pounds. Will occasionally be required to pull/push 500 to 1000 pounds (wheeled carts). While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand majority of shift (concrete floor); walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; balance; climb ladder; stoop/bend; talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision; distance vision; color vision; peripheral vision; depth perception; and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Tools and Equipment: Must be able to use hand tools such as pitchfork, broom, hammer, chain breaker, pliers, screwdrivers, come-a-long, wire cutters; safe operation of vehicle to and from work area
  • Environment: Required to work in dimly lit area on wet, slippery surfaces and in hot, dry, dusty, wet, and cold environments.
  • Personal Protective Equipment Required: Safety goggles and/or glasses, face shield, chemical gloves, waterproof apron, and rubber boots are required when handling disinfectants. Must wear company provided facial covering. Ear plugs may be used as needed. NIOSH approved N95 particulate respirators may be worn as needed.
  • Chemicals Commonly Used: Disinfectants, cleaners, lubricants, spray foam, vehicle fluids.
  • Safety: Team member is expected to follow all applicable safety policies and procedures. These include but are not limited to Hazard Communication, Respiratory Protection, LOTO and Personal Protective Equipment. Team member is expected to identify, address and mitigate safety related risks.

1ST SHIFT (United States of America)
