title: Engineer Senior
description:
Department: Charlotte Area Transit System Department

Salary: $89,552.00 - $128,730.99 Commensurate with Experience

Thank you for your interest in joining the team that keeps Charlotte moving, at a very exciting time for our organization. At the Charlotte Area Transit System (CATS), we’re committed to delivering safe, reliable, and innovative transit services for our growing community, and we value employees who bring professionalism, passion, and a commitment to public service.

This position is currently employed by CATS, a department of the City of Charlotte. With the passage of the PAVE Act and last year’s sales tax referendum, CATS is preparing to transition from a City department to the newly created Metropolitan Public Transit Authority (MPTA). The MPTA was established to strengthen regional transit governance, improve accountability, and support long‑term investment in mobility. It’s an important and exciting step forward for transit in our region.

Employees hired into this role will remain City employees through December 31, 2026, and will transition to MPTA employment on January 1, 2027. Benefits and compensation will follow City provisions through 2026 and shift to MPTA provisions in 2027, with clear information shared in advance. Your core duties, reporting structure, and daily responsibilities will remain consistent, with no break in service. If anything delays the transition, your City employment, including compensation and benefits, will remain in place until the move to the MPTA occurs.

The creation of the MPTA positions us for a more modern, sustainable, and efficient transit system, one that can better support the Charlotte region for decades to come. We’re excited about what’s ahead and appreciate your interest in being part of it.

SUMMARY

The Senior Engineer plans, organizes, reviews, and directs engineering work performed by consultants and departmental staff while providing advanced technical expertise for the development, design, and delivery of rail transit projects in coordination with internal divisions, City departments, State and Federal agencies, and other stakeholders.

Assigned to the team for the Silver Line Light Rail project, as well as other projects as directed, the Senior Engineer plays a key role in supporting the planning, design, and execution of a major light rail transit investment, pursuing funding under the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) Capital Investment Grant (CIG) program. This position provides advanced engineering expertise, technical oversight, and cross disciplinary coordination to ensure the project complies with all regulatory, design, safety, quality, cost, and schedule requirements essential for successful execution.

The Senior Engineer also represents the Silver Line project and Charlotte Area Transit System (CATS) Development at technical project coordination meetings and in public outreach efforts, participating in public meetings, community engagement sessions, and stakeholder presentations as necessary.

Major Duties and Responsibilities

  • Play a key role in overseeing engineering activities for light rail infrastructure, systems, and facilities, including trackwork, civil/structural elements, stations, utilities, and rail systems.
  • Serve as technical subject matter expert reviewing consultant and contractor engineering submittals, drawings, calculations, and specifications.
  • Ensure project compliance with FTA CIG requirements, including environmental commitments, design criteria, risk management processes, and project controls.
  • Coordinate the organizational and stakeholder review of major project milestones, including design submittals and construction bid documents, as well as associated comment resolution processes.
  • Support development and maintenance of FTA-required documents such as the Project Management Plan, Quality Program, Safety and Security Certification Plan, and supporting technical documentation.
  • Collaborate with internal departments and external partners including municipal agencies, utility companies, regulatory bodies, and community stakeholders.
  • Resolve design conflicts efficiently through collaborative problem solving.
  • Provide engineering guidance during project development, engineering, and implementation to ensure constructability, operational efficiency, maintainability, and long-term lifecycle value of project components.
  • Evaluate and respond to development and property owner inquiries along the Silver Line corridor.
  • Provide thorough private development entitlement reviews in compliance with local regulatory agency requirements to ensure compliance with CATS and Silver Line requirements.
  • Participate in contract procurement activities including approving/editing technical documents, evaluating proposals, and supporting contract negotiations.
  • Monitor construction activities, support field engineering, and resolve technical issues, including change management and verification of contractor work quality.
  • Assist in identifying, evaluating, communicating, and mitigating project risks throughout the course of the project, in compliance with FTA requirements.
  • Prepare engineering reports, presentations, and documentation for agency leadership, oversight bodies, and FTA representatives.
  • Represent the Silver Line project and the transit agency during public outreach efforts, including public meetings, open houses, community workshops, and stakeholder briefings.
  • Communicate complex engineering concepts clearly to non‑technical audiences, ensuring public understanding of project goals, impacts, and benefits.
  • Mentor junior engineers and contribute to the development of agency engineering standards, procedures, and best practices.
  • As part of your responsibility to support the CATS Safety Culture, report safety concerns and issues through the various methods established by CATS as outlined in the ASP.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Strong understanding of engineering principles related to infrastructure design and construction
  • Ability to interpret and apply FTA regulations, CIG program requirements, and federal/state/local engineering standards.
  • Skilled in reviewing and commenting on complex engineering design packages, technical specifications, and construction documentation.
  • Knowledge of project management, project controls, cost estimating, scheduling, and risk assessment methodologies.
  • Ability to assess constructability, maintainability, and systems integration across multidisciplinary project components.
  • Experience preparing and delivering presentations for both technical and non‑technical audiences.
  • Strong problem‑solving abilities and aptitude for resolving technical issues in design and construction.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks, prioritize competing demands, and meet project deadlines.
  • Effective communication skills for collaboration with technical teams, stakeholders, and regulatory partners.
  • Ability to clearly explain engineering concepts to the public, elected officials, and community groups in non-technical language.
  • Strong interpersonal skills and comfort participating in public meetings, community engagement activities, and stakeholder discussions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working on or managing rail transit or major transportation capital projects.
  • Experience directing and/or managing consultants or contractor work.
  • Direct experience with FTA CIG program requirements and processes.
  • Experience participating in public outreach or presenting engineering concepts to community groups.
  • Familiarity with NEPA, environmental permitting, and safety/security certification processes.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or a related field.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) license.
  • 10 years of relevant engineering experience in transportation, infrastructure, or transit projects.
  • Demonstrated experience working on multidisciplinary engineering projects requiring coordination across teams.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills are essential.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

The City’s Background Check Policy requires background checks to be conducted on final internal or external candidate(s) applying for any position with the City of Charlotte. The type of information that will be collected as part of a background check includes, but is not limited to: reference checks, social security verification, education verification, criminal conviction record check, and, if applicable, a credit history check, sex offender registry and motor vehicle records check.

Background checks must be in compliance with all federal and state statutes, such as the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA). The checks must be consistent with the guidelines set forth by these laws requiring organizations to obtain a candidate’s written authorization before obtaining a criminal background report, motor vehicle records check or credit report; and to properly store and dispose of information derived from such reports.

Final candidates must pass a pre-employment drug-screening test and physical examination. During the selection process, candidates may be asked to take a skills test, and/or participate in other assessments.

DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS

28 September 2026-23:59-GMT+01:00 Central European Time (Rome)

WFP celebrates and embraces diversity. It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.


ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.


At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.

  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.

  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

JOB TITLE: Disability Inclusion Officer
TYPE OF CONTRACT: Consultant level III
UNIT/DIVISION: Gender Protection and Inclusion Unit/ PO
DUTY STATION (City, Country): Rome/ Italy or remote
DURATION: 11 months

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian agency, fighting hunger worldwide. We are seeking to fill the position of Disability Inclusion Officer based at our Headquarters in Rome, Italy or remotely. WFP is well-known for its ability to deliver food assistance rapidly to people in need. In order to respond effectively in the challenging contexts in which WFP operates, staff require sound knowledge of the fundamentals of programming, as well as skills in specialized areas, such as humanitarian access, protection, accountability to affected populations (AAP), and conflict sensitive programming. The Gender, Protection and Inclusion (GPI) team at WFP Headquarters supports the integration of gender equality, protection and inclusion considerations across WFP’s policies, programmes and operations. This includes strengthening how evidence is generated, analysed and used to inform programme design, implementation, and corporate reporting, and ensuring that people-centred approaches are consistently reflected across the programme cycle. The Programme Quality and Excellence team within GPI ensures that high standards of each thematic area covered by GPI, including Disability Inclusion, remain adequately addressed in WFP’s programmes and operations. Under the overall supervision of the Senior Disability Inclusion Advisor, the Disability Inclusion Officer will undertake the following duties

ACCOUNTABILITIES/RESPONSIBILITIES:

Five workstreams

Engagement with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs)

  • Lead OPD engagement work on behalf of WFP.
  • Develop and foster partnerships with OPDs on behalf of WFP at the global and regional level that are mutually beneficial to both WFP and OPD partners.
  • Update guidelines and roll-out for consultation with persons with disabilities, namely through their representative organizations, that ensure accessibility and inclusiveness, and promote representation of the diversity of persons with disabilities and intersectionality.
  • Streamline systems for consultation with OPDs globally, including through direct contributions to the BHA project - Outcome 2 – Engage as well as other aspects of the Localization Portfolio insofar as they relate to Disability Inclusion.
  • In collaboration with the Partnerships division, review and update field level agreements and/or other partnership frameworks to reflect the relationship with OPDs.

Accessibility

  • Work across support GHQ and CO functions to provide support on accessibility related topics including through the ED Assurance Framework and as part of WFP minimum programming standards.
  • Promote accessibility of the built environment at WFP headquarters and across country offices through establishment and implementation of standards and guidance.
  • Support completion of ICT accessibility assessment and progress of implementation of emanating recommendations.
  • Support with baseline assessment and subsequent approach for ensuring accessibility of Conferences and Services in collaboration with the Conference Servicing Unit

Supporting Country Offices and Global HQ Regions

  • Provide technical assistance and capacity building to Regionally Outposted Colleagues and COs, in partnership with cross-cutting Protection, AAP, Gender and/or Disability Inclusion regional or CO advisors.
  • Support and provide technical support to at least one Regional Office to develop and manage their DI work plans, including Regional/ CO workplans. Provide back-up support for a second Regional Office.
  • Support DI mainstreaming throughout Country Strategic Plans through the FAR (CSP); data collection and utilization for CSP development, Annual Country Reporting and CRF reporting.

Cross Functional

  • Provide guidance to the Steering Committee and the Working Group in relevant policy and technical areas with respect to the deliverables particularly in relation to the roll out of UNDIS 2.0
  • Deliver accessible trainings on consultation with OPDs, accessibility, reasonable accommodation and other related topics reflected in this TOR.
  • Participate in relevant employee resources groups or working groups related to disability inclusion as well as to the Community of Practice for DI.
  • Contribute to future strategy development on disability inclusion including capacity strengthening plans.

People Operations/Human Resources

  • Provide technical support and recommendations to Human Resources on Reasonable Accommodation through rolling out the Reasonable Accommodation guidance and policy in line with the Diversity & Inclusion team requests.
  • Provide strategic inputs and guidance to existing human resources policies and processes from the disability inclusion perspective, as requested.
  • Embed disability inclusion throughout end-to-end recruitment cycle to increase employment of persons with disabilities at WFP.
  • Work with recruiters and human resources globally to enhance knowledge, capacity and practices on recruitment, retention and career development.
  • Assist with capacity building initiatives (on-line and in person) as well as advocacy materials in co-ordination with the Diversity and Inclusion Team

DELIVERABLES AT THE END OF THE CONTRACT:

  • Update guidance note on enabling persons with disabilities to participate in all processes that that assess, plan, design, implement, monitor and evaluate WFP operations and programming, at the headquarters, regional and country levels in line with GPI minimum standards as well as UNDIS 2.0 programme standards and FAR integration
  • Partnerships with key representative OPDs at the global, regional and country office levels including those set up through the Engage programme and relevant contracting mechansims
  • Project plan for Regional Roll outs of concerned ROs including budget, timelines and monitoring information with action plans and reporting on all Country Office progress within the selected Regions.
  • Technical assistance to COs on GPI minimum standards as well as specific technical advice provided on targeted DI interventions. These will be categorized through assistance for the Integrated Context Analysis and Risk Assessment tool, the FAR, the Gender Equality Certification Programme + DI and other GPI corporate processes.
  • Training on all new UNDIS indicators through the DIWG Focal Points system, the Disability Inclusion Network and the COP-DI

QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED:

Education:

Masters degree in one or more of the following disciplines: social sciences, development studies, international relations, sociology or other relevant field.

Experience:

  • At least six years of progressively responsible professional experience in development projects or humanitarian assistance, of which at least two dedicated to disability inclusion.
  • Demonstrated field and policy-oriented experience working on disability inclusion is required.
  • Experience in operational research and programme design in the areas covered under this TOR is desirable.


Knowledge & Skills:

  • Demonstrated knowledge of the normative framework on Disability Inclusion;
  • Experience in coordination is required;
  • Experience on guidance and training development is an asset;
  • Previous UN experience, preferably with WFP, is highly desirable;
  • Demonstrated strong analytical and writing skills;
  • Ability to write in an engaging and informative manner, and conceptualize and clearly synthesize information;
  • Ability to work on short timelines, under pressure, and managing multiple priorities simultaneously with minimal supervision; and
  • Initiative, enthusiasm, creativity, and flexibility with excellent interpersonal skills and team spirit.

Languages:

Fluency in English is required, knowledge of another UN language is strongly desirable.

WFP LEADERSHIP FRAMEWORK

WFP Leadership Framework guides to the common standards of behavior that guide HOW we work together to accomplish our mission.

Click here to access WFP Leadership Framework

REASONABLE ACCOMMODATION

WFP is committed to supporting individuals with disabilities by providing reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process. If you require a reasonable accommodation, please contact: global.inclusion@wfp.org

NO FEE DISCLAIMER

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

REMINDERS BEFORE YOU SUBMIT YOUR APPLICATION

  • All applications must be submitted exclusively through our online recruiting system. We do not consider CVs or applications sent by email, LinkedIn, or any other channel.

  • We strongly recommend that your Workday profile is accurate and complete, and that all sections are filled in, including your employment history, academic qualifications, language skills, and UN grade (if applicable). Once your profile is completed, please apply, and submit your application.

  • If you experience technical issues while submitting your application, you may contact us at global.hrerecruitment@wfp.org. Please note that this email is only for technical issues with an application - unsolicited applications or documents sent to this inbox will not receive a reply.

  • At the application stage, the only required documents are your CV and Cover Letter. Additional documents (passport, certificates, recommendation letters, etc.) may be requested later in the process.

  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and invited to proceed to the next stage of the recruitment process.

All employment decisions are made on the basis of organizational needs, job requirements, merit, and individual qualifications. WFP is committed to providing an inclusive work environment free of sexual exploitation and abuse, all forms of discrimination, any kind of harassment, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. Therefore, all selected candidates will undergo rigorous reference and background checks.


No appointment under any kind of contract will be offered to members of the UN Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions (ACABQ), International Civil Service Commission (ICSC), FAO Finance Committee, WFP External Auditor, WFP Audit Committee, Joint Inspection Unit (JIU) and other similar bodies within the United Nations system with oversight responsibilities over WFP, both during their service and within three years of ceasing that service.

title: Leader, Semiconductor NPI SCPM and Ramp Planning
description:
The application window is expected to close on: 09/24/2026

Meet the Team

The Semiconductor NPI & Ramp Planning team serves as the operational quarterback for new product introductions, ensuring alignment across Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing, and external partners. We are accountable for planning and execution across the entire pre-production lifecycle, from initial prototype builds post-tapeout through EVT, DVT, pilot, and initial production ramp. Our high-performing Supply Chain Program Managers (SCPMs) own product execution from Execute Commit through Production Launch and Ramp Stabilization. We drive predictable execution in a fast-paced technology environment, managing complex programs and influencing across organizational boundaries. By leading supply chain program management, prototype execution, and silicon operations, we enable predictable launches and ensure a seamless transition into sustaining operations.

Your Impact

As the Leader of Semiconductor NPI & Ramp Planning, you will lead, mentor, and develop a team of Supply Chain Program Managers responsible for product execution from Executive Commit through production launch. You will establish organizational priorities, operating mechanisms, and performance expectations that drive accountability and execution excellence. By translating executive business commitments into actionable supply chain, manufacturing, and program execution plans, you will drive cross-functional leadership and alignment across Product Management, Engineering, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Operations, Finance, and Quality organizations. You will lead supply chain planning for engineering builds, manage semiconductor operations and foundry management relationships, and oversee prototype silicon execution through foundries and OSAT partners. Additionally, you will develop and execute supply chain ramp strategies, drive risk management and mitigation, and establish scalable New Product Introduction (NPI) and ramp planning processes that improve launch predictability and operational excellence.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelors Degree, Also requires 5-10+ years of supervisory experience in a people leader role.
  • Demonstrated success leading complex product introductions and manufacturing ramps in the semiconductor industry.
  • Experience managing supply chain execution across global suppliers, contract manufacturers, and technology partners.
  • Deep understanding of the semiconductor supply chain with direct experience in foundry operations, wafer starts, silicon qualification, and OSAT.
  • Strong knowledge of supply planning, capacity planning, demand planning, inventory management, and S&OP processes.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with ERP, MRP, and planning systems.
  • APICS/ASCM certification or comparable credentials.
  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills.
  • Proven people leadership ability to foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, urgency, and continuous improvement.

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

description:
About the role:

Friet, ijsjes, snacks en veel verschillende gasten. In de snackbar van Landal Het Vennenbos is er altijd iets te doen. Zoek je een bijbaan naast school of studie waarin je lekker bezig bent, samenwerkt met collega's en direct werkervaring opdoet? Dan is dit een leuke plek om te starten.

title: Technology Development Engineering Intern
description:
Technology Development Engineer Intern

Location: Bloomington, MN| [On-Site]


Employment Type: Temporary – 12-13 weeks

About the Role

The Development Engineering Intern will report to the Lead Engineer in the Technology Development and Transfer group to support new development efforts.

Key Responsibilities

  • Characterize electrical parametric devices by hand probe

  • Perform and evaluate process splits

  • Measure and analyze inline wafer data (film thickness, critical dimensions, etc.)

  • Create process characterization documents

  • Support company initiatives, such as; quality, safety and environmental management, CQI, 5S, yield management, cost containment and perform other duties as assigned.

  • Other duties, as assigned

​

Qualifications
Required:

  • Students working toward a Bachelor or Masters degree in Electrical Engineering or Physics

  • Students in their Junior year or higher

  • Excellent attention to detail

  • Strong verbal and written communication skills

Preferred:

  • Coursework should include: Intro to Device Physics and/or Semiconductor Processing course

About Us

At Polar Semiconductor, we’re on a mission to fulfill our future as the U.S. based manufacturing partner of choice for differentiated power and sensor technologies. With a $525M investment from the CHIPs Act, the state of Minnesota, and private equity, we are looking for the best in the industry to help Polar transform from a captive fab to a pure-play foundry. We are doubling our manufacturing capacity and investing in advanced BCD and Wide Bandgap technology such as GaN. Polar has a long history in manufacturing automotive grade semiconductors and we are expanding in strategic markets such as national defense and AI data centers. We pride ourselves on state-of-the-art semiconductor manufacturing, a collaborative culture, and a commitment to helping our customers succeed.

What We Offer:

Salary: $25.50 - $32.20 per hour. Pay offered is based on many factors including, but not limited to, the job-related experience, skills, education, and credentials of each candidate.


Benefits & Other Eligible Compensation: Includes 401(k) plan and paid time off.

Polar Semiconductor is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. We are committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all employees and to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.

About Minneapolis/St. Paul Area

Our offices and manufacturing facility are located in Bloomington, Minnesota, a suburb of Minneapolis. Living in the Minneapolis / Saint Paul area offers a strong sense of community, a vibrant arts and music scene, and abundant outdoor activities year-round. The city boasts a lower cost of living than many major metros, excellent parks and lakes, and a well-educated workforce with diverse job opportunities. Its distinct seasons bring variety, from colorful autumns to lively summers filled with festivals and waterfront activities.

title: Security Supervisor
description:
Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong is looking for a Security Supervisor to join our Security team.

Are you a master of craft? Do you thrive in a team that succeeds together, demonstrating integrity and respect while acting responsibly? Do you embrace a growth mindset? We invite you to become a fan of the exceptional.

Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group is the award-winning owner and operator of some of the most luxurious hotels, resorts and residences located in prime destinations around the world, with a strong development pipeline. Increasingly recognised for creating some of the world’s most sought-after properties, the Group provides legendary service inspired by Asian heritage whilst representing the very cutting-edge of luxury experiences.

Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong is the group's flagship hotel, and an icon in its own right. Having delighted guests with award-winning service and impressive facilities since 1963, it is the much-loved address for those seeking an exclusive sanctuary in the heart of this exciting metropolis. Besides 447 luxurious guest rooms and suites, the hotel features a Club Lounge as well as an extensive SPA and wellness area. In addition to its 13 banqueting spaces, Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong is home to nine highly individual bars and restaurants, including much-loved greats and one Michelin-star venue, offering guests a series of elevated dining experiences This iconic hotel is the epitome of contemporary luxury combined with Oriental heritage. We believe that our colleagues play an integral role in our success and are committed to providing a caring, motivating and rewarding working environment.

In additional, Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong is embarking upon a transformative renovation with an investment over USD100 million and will be unveiling new and enhanced offerings incorporating new elegant guest accommodation designs, and the introduction of exciting dining and wellness experiences, including the arrival of globally renowned chefs, Daniel Boulud and Daniele Cason in 2026.

About the job

Based at the Mandarin Oriental, Hong Kong within Security Department in Hong Kong, the Security Supervisor is responsible for completing responsibilities for hotel as security needed. The Security Supervisor reports to the Security Manager.

As Security Supervisor, you will be responsible for the following duties:

  • Provide supervisory guidance and support to all Security Officers;
  • Perform Hotel security daily duties such as access control, regular patrol and incident handling;
  • Arrange the duties for the shift and be responsible for the efficient discharge of duties by subordinates;
  • Assist in the development and implementation of Standard Operating Procedures for the Department;
  • Respond to all accidents and assist guests / staff during emergency situations;
  • Prepare, review and follow-up on all incident, loss and accident reports;
  • Monitor CCTV, Perimeter-Alarm System, and Fire Life Safety System;
  • Protect and safeguard all guests and staff, their belongings and all hotel assets.

As Security Supervisor, we expect from you:

  • At least 3 to 5 years related working experience;
  • Experienced in report writing and in carrying out investigations;
  • Knowledge of CCTV, BMS & AFA systems;
  • Honest, Self-motivated and Responsible;
  • Holder of valid Security Personnel Permit;
  • Holder of First Aid, CPR and AED Training is an advantage;
  • Fluent in Cantonese, and basic English & Mandarin;
  • Shift duty is required.

Our commitment to you

  • Learning & Development. Your success is our success. We craft unique learning and development programmes for various stages in your career so that you grow, continuously.
  • MOstay. When you work as hard as our colleagues do, it’s important to take time off. As a member of the #MOfamily, you can stay with us wherever you go in the world. The MOstay programme offers complimentary nights and additionally attractive rates on rooms for you and your loved ones.
  • Health & Colleague Wellness. Finding the right worklife balance is important. Your wellbeing matters to us. A variety of health benefits and wellness programmes are offered to all our colleagues, globally.
  • Retirement Plans. When you show commitment to us, we reciprocate. We offer different retirement plans depending on the length of your service and your role.

We’re Fans. Are you?

title: Credit Officer I – Global Infrastructure Credit
description:
Job Description:

At Bank of America, we are guided by a common purpose to help make financial lives better through the power of every connection. We do this by driving Responsible Growth and delivering for our clients, teammates, communities and shareholders every day.

Being a Great Place to Work and providing a culture of caring is core to how we drive Responsible Growth. We are intentional about fostering an inclusive workplace where every teammate has the opportunity to succeed, build a career and contribute to our shared success. This includes attracting and developing exceptional talent, recognizing and rewarding performance, and supporting our teammates’ physical, emotional, and financial wellness through affordable, competitive and flexible benefits.

We value the unique perspectives individuals bring from all backgrounds and career paths - whether shaped by military service, community college education, or a wide range of work and life experiences. These journeys foster resilience, leadership and innovation, strengthening our workforce and positively impact the communities we serve.

Bank of America is committed to an in-office culture that supports collaboration, engagement, and career development. Our approach includes clear in-office expectations, while providing an appropriate level of flexibility based on role-specific responsibilities and business needs.

At Bank of America, you can build a successful career with opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact. Join us!

Job Description:
This job is responsible for managing clients and related credit products, partnering closely with relationship management, sales/trading, treasury management, operations and risk teams to support the client relationship. Key responsibilities include underwriting, monitoring, managing operational needs and/or client requests. Job expectations include credit-focused client management responsibilities, independent thought leadership, and the ability to provide feedback to less experienced teammates.

Embedded across the bank’s eight lines of business, the Global Infrastructure Credit team reflects the bank’s initiative to fuel the global economy, build trust and credibility with communities, and represents a company that people want to work for, invest in, and do business with. The Global Infrastructure Credit team supports the continued growth in sustainable and infrastructure finance and further deliver on Bank of America’s Critical Infrastructure Finance Initiative. The Global Infrastructure Credit Team covers transactions for Project Finance, Tax Equity and Corporate Lending through involvement in the origination and underwriting of transactions.

Responsibilities:

  • Partners with relationship management and product partners to assess clients’ credit needs and create solutions
  • Leads loan structure conversations and negotiates loan documentation with clients and internal/external legal partners
  • Drives credit and risk approval processes for new credit originations, renewals, increases, and modifications
  • Mentors and supports associates
  • Support the underwriting and documentation of project finance and other credit facilities, ensuring alignment with client needs and the bank’s risk/return objectives
  • Support the financial modeling, loan structure, industry, economic, and other analyses to support the loan decision-making process
  • Ensures adherence to credit policies, guidelines, procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements
  • Perform financial, industry, counterparty, and transaction analyses, including qualitative and quantitative due diligence to support underwriting decisions
  • Support the reviews of the credit profile of key transaction counterparties (e.g., borrowers, sponsors, servicers, and off takers) and assess structural and stress considerations
  • Monitors the client's operating performance and financial condition, proactively identifying issues and opportunities

Required Qualifications:

  • 8 + years of experience in commercial banking or finance industry with significant credit, tax equity, and infrastructure/energy project finance experience.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Master’s Degree (MBA). Engineering, mathematics or other technical degrees will be considered with an MBA
  • Strong understanding of financial models and analysis
  • Extensive experience in analysis and management of highly complex, project-oriented transactions (tax equity and debt), including problem solving. Demonstrated aptitude for reviewing, understanding and interpreting associated transaction documents and project contracts.
  • Strong credit and risk analysis skills, including experience in commercial and large corporate credit analysis.
  • Ability to work efficiently and productively on several transactions or tasks at one time.
  • Ability to interact effectively with internal and external clients and partners. Experience mentoring junior associates.
  • Clear and articulate oral and written communication skills.
  • Formal credit training program at financial institution

Skills:

  • Analytical Thinking
  • Credit and Risk Assessment
  • Financial Analysis
  • Research Analysis
  • Underwriting
  • Attention to Detail
  • Business Acumen
  • Financial Forecasting and Modeling
  • Loan Structuring
  • Written Communications
  • Business Development
  • Collaboration
  • Critical Thinking
  • Portfolio Analysis
  • Stakeholder Management

description:
Job Details:

Position Summary

The Gate Attendant Lead supports safe, secure, and efficient access-control operations at the Tyson Berry Street facility. In addition to performing gate attendant duties, this position provides day-to-day guidance to assigned Gate Attendants and Scale House Operators, coordinates shift activities and coverage, reinforces standard procedures, and serves as the first point of escalation for routine operational concerns. The Lead monitors the movement of Team Members, visitors, vendors, contractors, truck drivers, vehicles, trailers, and materials entering or leaving the facility and supports Scale House operations. Responsibilities include capturing and recording truck and trailer weights, entering load and manifest information, printing and maintaining weigh tickets, conducting lot checks, communicating lot changes, and reporting equipment, maintenance, safety, or operational concerns. The Lead maintains accurate records, communicates with plant management and external partners, and helps ensure compliance with company safety, security, access-control, and Scale House requirements. This position escalates disciplinary, staffing, safety, security, emergency, and significant operational matters to the appropriate supervisor or manager when necessary.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide daily work direction and operational support to Gate Attendants and Scale House personnel while promoting consistent, professional application of site procedures.

  • Coordinate assignments, breaks, shift handoffs, and available coverage; promptly notify supervision of staffing gaps or operational concerns.

  • Assist with onboarding, job-specific training, coaching, and procedure refreshers for Gate Attendants and assigned Scale House personnel.

  • Verify that required gate and Scale House logs, visitor and vehicle records, weigh tickets, inspection forms, load sheets, manifest sheets, driver schedules, keys, badges, radios, and other assigned records or equipment are complete, accurate, and properly transferred between shifts.

  • Monitor and control the entry and exit of Team Members, visitors, vendors, contractors, truck drivers, vehicles, trailers, and materials in accordance with company requirements.

  • Verify identification, credentials, appointments, delivery information, and access authorization before granting entry.

  • Operate the Scale House computer system and associated equipment to capture incoming, outgoing, empty, farm, shrink, final, and other required truck or trailer weights.

  • Enter required information accurately in the Scale House management system and applicable manifest, incoming-load, and driver-schedule records; print, record, and distribute weigh tickets as required.

  • Conduct and document assigned trailer and lot checks and report discrepancies, damage, suspicious activity, or safety concerns.

  • Inspect live-haul cages or modules upon arrival for visible damage and promptly notify Live Receiving management when concerns are identified.

  • Notify plant supervision and USDA of lot changes in accordance with established procedures.

  • Communicate by telephone and radio with drivers, plant management, Live Receiving or Evisceration supervision, USDA, transportation partners, and other departments as needed to support efficient operations.

  • Monitor items brought into and removed from the facility and escalate suspected policy violations or unauthorized activity.

  • Respond to routine gate or Scale House concerns, complaints, access issues, equipment problems, alarms, and incidents; follow emergency procedures and contact supervision, maintenance, or emergency responders when required.

  • Report observed plant, Scale House, security, or equipment issues to the appropriate management or maintenance contact.

  • Maintain confidentiality and safeguard company information, records, keys, badges, and access-control resources.

  • Keep the gatehouse, Scale House, and assigned work areas organized, professional, and ready for continuous operations.

  • Model professional conduct, customer service, reliability, and compliance with safety and security expectations.

  • Perform Gate Attendant or Scale House duties during breaks, absences, emergencies, or periods of increased activity.

  • Complete other duties as assigned by supervision.

Qualifications and Requirements:

Education: High school diploma or GED preferred.

Experience: At least 6 months of gate attendant, security, access-control, or related experience preferred. Previous lead, trainer, or shift-coordination experience is preferred.

Computer and Equipment Skills: Proficiency with computers and the ability to learn and accurately operate access-control, visitor-management, communication, recordkeeping, and Scale House systems and associated equipment. Must be able to enter data accurately, capture vehicle and trailer weights, and print and maintain weigh tickets and related operational records.

Communication and Leadership Skills: Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills. Must be able to provide clear direction, coach others respectfully, manage multiple priorities, resolve routine concerns, remain calm and professional during stressful situations, and communicate effectively by radio and telephone with drivers, plant supervision, USDA, transportation partners, and other departments.

Working Conditions: Work is performed in guard shack and Scale House environments and may require periodic outdoor activity in hot, cold, wet, or changing weather conditions. The position requires sustained attention in a high-traffic environment, frequent use of phones, radios, computers, and Scale House equipment, and the ability to safely complete assigned lot checks and inspections.

Position-Specific Requirements: Must maintain dependable attendance and punctuality; demonstrate sound judgment, attention to detail, integrity, and a positive work ethic; follow all company safety, security, confidentiality, and conduct requirements; complete required in-house training; and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Must have and maintain excellent attendance; No serious disciplinary; No serious Safety violations; specialized in-house training is required.

Schedule: This position is responsible for leading Gate Attendant and Scale House operations across B Shift and D Shift, which provide facility coverage from 6:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m., Sunday through Saturday. The Lead may rotate between Gate Attendant and Scale House assignments to support absences, breaks, emergencies, or operational needs and will be required to remain available for on-call response to issues affecting the assigned shifts.

Travel: None

title: Programme Policy Officer (Head of Programme) NO-B Sittwe
description:
DEADLINE FOR APPLICATIONS

23 September 2026-23:59-GMT+06:30 Myanmar Time (Yangon)

It is committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity for all its employees and encourages qualified candidates to apply irrespective of race, colour, national origin, ethnic or social background, genetic information, gender, gender identity and/or expression, sexual orientation, religion or belief, HIV status or disability.


ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.


At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

To learn more about WFP, visit our website: and follow us on social media to keep up with our latest news: YouTube, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, TikTok.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

  • WFP offers a highly inclusive, diverse, and multicultural working environment.

  • WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.

  • A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.

  • We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).

THE ROLE

The Programme Policy Officer (Head of Programme) plays a key role in supporting the effective implementation of programme activities across the Rakhine Area Office by ensuring strong coordination, monitoring, reporting, and engagement with cooperating partners. The position focuses on providing operational oversight, ensuring compliance with established procedures, and maintaining quality assurance standards across all programme interventions. The Programme Policy Officer (Head of Programme) is responsible for the overall management and coordination of programme activities, including monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions and cooperating partner management, to ensure the timely, efficient, and high-quality delivery of programme outputs in line with organizational objectives and expected results.

KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES (not all-inclusive, within delegated authority):

Support the Head of Area Office in ensuring the timely achievement of monthly implementation targets and programme objectives.

  • Provide technical guidance and operational support for all programme activities implemented under the Area Office.

  • Coordinate the day-to-day planning, design, implementation, monitoring, and budget management of programme interventions.

  • Identify operational risks and implementation challenges, including Transfer Authorization (TA) constraints, access issues, Hundi-related challenges, and Field Level Agreement (FLA) requirements, and develop appropriate mitigation measures.

  • Manage and coordinate all FLA processes to ensure agreements are finalized and approved prior to programme implementation and distributions.

  • Lead caseload planning and resource allocation based on vulnerability analysis, beneficiary targeting criteria, approved caseloads, and available resources.

  • Monitor Cooperating Partners’ (CP) performance against agreed targets and quality standards, and support the implementation of partner improvement and capacity-strengthening plans.

  • Review commodity stock levels and distribution requirements, forecast potential shortages, initiate call-forward requests, facilitate TA processes, and coordinate with the Country Office on commodity and ration adjustments.

  • Plan, oversee, and monitor beneficiary verification, targeting exercises, and Community Engagement Mechanism (CEM) activities to ensure accountability and programme integrity.

  • Ensure achievement of Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) targets, including the verification and timely resolution of 100 percent of CEM cases through effective coordination with cooperating partners.

  • Coordinate and facilitate joint programming initiatives and collaborative activities with UN agencies, NGOs, government counterparts, and other stakeholders.

  • Prepare and submit monthly distribution plans and implementation schedules for review and approval by the Country Office.

  • Strengthen the technical and operational capacity of Area Office staff and cooperating partners through coaching, mentoring, training needs assessments, and the delivery of orientation and capacity-building sessions.

  • Support emergency preparedness and response activities, including anticipatory action planning, emergency assessments, and coordination with cooperating partners during emergency operations.

  • Represent WFP at sub-national coordination forums, technical working groups, partner meetings, and Country Office coordination meetings, as required.

  • Facilitate the preparation, consolidation, and timely submission of programme reports for government counterparts and the Country Office, ensuring receipt and review of all cooperating partner quarterly and final reports.

  • Maintain effective coordination with internal and external stakeholders to ensure programme compliance, accountability, and achievement of expected results.

  • Guide and supervise more junior staff, acting as a point of referral and supporting them with analysis and queries.

  • Act on behalf of the Head of Area Office during periods of absence, ensuring continuity of programme management, coordination, decision-making, and implementation oversight.

  • Other as required.

QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE


Education: Advanced University degree in business/public administration, finance, accounting, international development, audit or other relevant field, or First University degree with additional two years of relevant work experience and/or training/courses in audit, performance and risk management or other related fields.


DESIRED EXPERIENCES FOR ENTRY INTO THE ROLE:

  • At least three or more years of relevant, progressively responsible experience in leading, undertaking and/or contributing to planning activities, or other relevant fields.

  • Has deepened technical knowledge through exposure to technical teams.

  • Has taken leadership of implementing programmes.

  • Has provided input into policy discussions and decisions.

  • Has emergency field experience

  • Has related management experience and oversight of external partners.

Language: Fluency in both spoken and written English and Burmese.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT

Type of contract: Fixed Term

Grade: NO-B

Number of Post: 1

Duration: 12 months

title: Risk and Audit Program Manager
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

Job Description

Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Risk Framework

Design, implement, and continuously refine an enterprise-wide risk mitigation framework covering all agency operations, programs, and business lines.

Develop and maintain a risk taxonomy and risk register in partnership with executive leadership. Establish key risk indicators (KRis) and reporting dashboards to monitor emerging risks in real time.

Internal Audit & Controls

Plan and execute a risk-based internal audit program, including scheduling, scoping, fieldwork, and reporting.

Evaluate the design and operating effectiveness of internal controls across lending, servicing, finance, IT, and program compliance functions.

Identify control gaps and partner with business unit leaders to develop corrective action plans; track remediation to closure.

Regulatory & Program Compliance Risk

Assess risks related to compliance with HUD, GSE (Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac), state housing finance regulations, bond covenants, and applicable federal/state fair lending and consumer protection laws.

Monitor changes in regulatory requirements and assess their impact on agency risk posture. Support external audits, regulatory examinations, and rating agency reviews.

Operational & Program Risk Assessment

Conduct periodic risk assessments across both single-family programs (homeownership lending, down payment assistance, mortgage servicing) and multifamily programs (loan underwriting, construction/permanent financing, asset management, rental assistance, bond issuance) to identify vulnerabilities.

Evaluate credit risk exposure and underwriting quality across the single-family and multifamily loan portfolios.

Evaluate third-party and vendor risk, including single-family mortgage servicers and originating lenders, multifamily loan servicers and property management agents, and contracted program administrators.

Assess fraud risk and support investigations as needed across both business lines.

Reporting & Governance

Prepare risk and audit reports for executive leadership, the Board, and/or Audit/Risk Committees.

Present findings, trends, and recommendations in clear, actionable formats for both technical and non-technical audiences.

Maintain documentation supporting audit trails, risk assessments, and control testing in accordance with professional standards (e.g., IIA Standards).

Culture & Training

Promote a strong risk-aware culture across the agency through training, policy development, and cross-departmental collaboration.

Serve as a subject matter resource to program and operations staff on risk identification and mitigation best practices.

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Public Administration, or a JD (Master's degree preferred).

7+ years of progressive experience in risk management, internal audit, or compliance, with at least 3 years in a supervisory/managerial capacity.

Experience finance strongly preferred, ideally spanning both single-family (mortgage banking, homeownership programs) and multifamily (affordable housing development, loan underwriting, asset management) business lines, or public finance more broadly.

Working knowledge of HUD, GSE, and/or state housing finance agency regulatory frameworks. Demonstrated experience building or managing enterprise risk frameworks (COSO ERM or similar).

Qualifications

Bachelor of Science, Experience (7-10 years)

Experience

Experience (7-10 years)

title: Nature Based Solutions Specialist
description:
Closing Date

2026-10-02

Job Title: Nature-based Solutions Specialist

Location: Within the Hampshire region (Hybrid/Flexible)

Contract Type: Permanent

Hours: 37, Monday to Friday

Salary: £45-48,000, depending on skills and experience

As part of Southern Water’s drive to enhance and protect the environment, the Environment & Innovation team are deploying the latest innovative solutions and working in partnership with our customers and stakeholders. The team takes a holistic approach to managing water quality and flow across the region, with a portfolio that has rapidly expanded from £50 million to over £2 billion in the next 10-year period. This is a fast-paced team that is now expanding to continue to deliver a larger programme of new and sustainable solutions.

A brand-new position has been created to join our Environment & Innovation team as a Nature-based Solutions Specialist.

About the role

Working within the Environment & Innovation department, this is a critical role underpinning the implementation of our Catchment Management strategies, which influence our 5 to 50 year strategic plans. The catchment management programme is driving environmental benefit via the delivery of our regulatory commitments such as the Water Industry National Environment Programme (WINEP) and statutory plans such as the Water Resource Management Plan, Drought Plan and Water Resources South East. The role will include a blend of desk and field-based work, with opportunities for site visits and on-site work across the chalk streams of Hampshire.

What you will be responsible for

  • You will support delivery of our regulatory programme, supporting the Principal Nature-based Solutions Specialist to technically manage implementation, delivery and reporting our regulatory investigations, impact assessments, ecological schemes and compliance requirements.
  • You will be responsible for undertaking technical evaluation / recommendations on environmental nature-based measures that will likely be needed to mitigate predicted environmental challenges from our operations.
  • You will provide Nature-based Solutions advice to the wider business in relation to ecology, planning and development, environmental policy etc.
  • You will contribute to industry forums promoting Southern Waters Catchment First approach.

What you’ll bring to the role

  • Demonstrable expertise in ecology, river / wetland restoration, biodiversity enhancement, Habitats Directive, Water Framework Directive, planning and development.
  • Proven expertise of technical report writing.
  • The ability to demonstrate the completion of quality multi-disciplinary tasks on time to a consistent & high standard.

description:

Job Description

Retail Keyholder: Buckhead

Shift Details: Part-Time

Who We Are

At Framebridge, we are disrupting the custom framing market by replacing a cumbersome experience with a delightful one. Our mission is to make framing so delightful, customers are inspired to frame everything they love—big, little and in between. We've framed over three million pieces and counting. We are building a beloved brand, and to be successful, we have to build a great team across a number of disciplines – ecommerce, retail, design, and manufacturing.

We are a consumer business operating online and in our growing fleet of retail stores. We operate multiple manufacturing studios that allow us to deliver a high-quality custom product at an affordable price with a quick turnaround. We exist, grow, and ultimately own the market by delighting customers who trust and value us.

The Role

We're seeking a Keyholder who will bring energy, leadership, and a customer-first attitude to our store team. As a trusted leader on the floor, you'll take on key-holding responsibilities while delivering the kind of experience that keeps customers coming back. This role reports to the Store Manager.

As a Framebridge Team Member, You Will:

Show Pride

We stand behind our work, we sweat the details, and we strive for continuous improvement every day. We're proud to frame the things you love, and show pride in our product and craftsmanship.

Adapt & Act

We are creative and solution-oriented, flexible, and proactive. We adapt and act quickly, embracing an environment of constant change.

Embrace Challenges

We embrace challenges with creative solutions and we know that collaboration is the only way to succeed. We set big goals and keep raising the bar together.

Secure the Baton

We take personal responsibility for delivering successful outcomes, not just completing tasks. We ensure every handoff is clear, complete, and sets the next teammates up to succeed.

Make It Special

We search everyday for opportunities to make our product and experience special. When you are building a business where every piece is priceless, making it special is core.

Build to Last

We are building a product and a business that are built to last. We work every day to build lasting relationships within our team and with our customers.

At Framebridge, our people are the heart of everything we build. We foster an inclusive, equitable, and collaborative environment where remarkable individuals take pride in their craft, elevate the customer experience, and are empowered to do the best work of their careers.

As a Keyholder, You Will:

  • Set the standard of offering exceptional customer service and representing the Framebridge brand in our retail stores

  • Support onboarding and training great retail team members

  • Execute and improve operational activities in our retail stores to ensure customer experience and financial goals are met

  • Apply excellent listening, oral, and communication skills to build relationships with our customers and coach retail team members

  • Demonstrate deep product knowledge and design advice to customers and train retail team members to do the same

  • Answer questions and troubleshoot issues using sound judgment

  • Offer suggestions to innovate and improve our retail experience

  • Help Framebridge deliver on our 100% happiness guarantee

  • Work a flexible schedule including evenings and weekends that meet the needs of the business

Who You Are:

  • Experience as a key holder in a customer service, retail, or hospitality role

  • An engaging personality with strong influence, interpersonal, communication, and relationship-building skills

  • Interest in design and excitement to work in a creative environment

  • Quick and eager learner of new tools, technology, products, and processes

  • Great time-management, organizational, and problem-solving skills

  • Adaptability and willingness to work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends

  • Degree in art, design, marketing or relevant fields preferred but not required

Physical Requirements:

This role requires the ability to perform the following physical tasks on a regular basis:

  • Standing for extended periods of time (up to 8 hours per shift)

  • Light lifting (up to 30 lbs) — carrying frames, supplies, or packaging materials

  • Bending, reaching, and light physical movement as needed in a retail or production environment

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role.

At Shell, supply chains are at the heart of our success, and our Contracts & Procurement team plays a critical role in keeping our business moving efficiently and competitively. Every day, the Downstream Contracts & Procurement organization manages approximately $40 million worth of non-hydrocarbon goods and services, helping to deliver value and support profitable business operations across the globe.

In this role, you will contribute to ensuring accurate and timely payments to our vendors, maintaining strong financial controls, and supporting reliable financial reporting. You will also help ensure compliance with company policies while upholding Shell’s commitment to integrity and operational excellence.

As a key member of the Accounts Payable team, you will act as a change champion, driving customer-focused solutions, applying your process expertise, and collaborating with colleagues across the organization to continuously improve the end-to-end Procure-to-Pay process. This is an excellent opportunity to make a meaningful impact while developing your career within a global and innovative company.

What you’ll be doing

As an Analyst, AP DRF, you will serve as a key partner to the business, building strong stakeholder relationships, resolving operational issues, and driving continuous improvement across the end-to-end Source-to-Pay (S2P) process.

  • Act as a subject matter expert (SME) and first point of escalation for Accounts Payable-related matters.
  • Collaborate with internal stakeholders and business partners to enhance service delivery, improve payment performance, and strengthen operational effectiveness.
  • Participate in operational meetings, projects, system enhancements, migrations, and digital transformation initiatives that support business objectives.
  • Contribute to a high-performing AP DRF team by sharing best practices and supporting organizational priorities.
  • Promote and uphold Shell's Health, Safety, Security, and Environment (HSSE) standards and culture.

What you bring

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • With experience in Accounts Payable, Finance Operations, or a related process environment.

Job Title: Site HR

Job Summary:
The Site HR is responsible for managing and executing HR and Administrative activities at the site level, ensuring smooth day-to-day operations, workforce discipline, and employee welfare. The role acts as a key connect between management, employees, and contract manpower — handling all HR & Admin related matters end-to-end (A to Z) at the site, while implementing group HR policies, processes, and practices in line with organizational goals.

Key Responsibilities:

Data Analysis & Decision Support – Prepares, analyzes, and interprets HR data and information to support management decision-making, and contributes to the development and implementation of HR policies, processes, programs, and practices.

Manpower Management – Handles overall manpower planning, deployment, and coordination at site, including recruitment, onboarding, attendance, and workforce availability, ensuring adequate staffing to meet operational requirements at all times.

Critical HR Issues & Discipline – Manages critical manpower concerns including disciplinary matters, grievances, conflicts, and misconduct cases; ensures fair and timely resolution in accordance with company policy and applicable labor laws, maintaining a disciplined and compliant work environment.

Employee Engagement & Development – Drives initiatives for employee engagement, motivation, training, performance evaluation, and rewards/recognition to build a committed and productive workforce.

Administration – Oversees site administration functions including facility management, contractor labor administration, statutory compliance, documentation, and liaison with local administration/government bodies as required.

End-to-End Site HR Ownership – Independently manages the complete spectrum of HR & Admin activities at the site (A to Z) — from manpower planning and welfare to compliance, discipline, and administration — ensuring uninterrupted HR support to site operations.

Advisory Support to Managers – Acts as a trusted advisor to site managers, providing guidance and recommendations on people-related matters to support effective decision-making.

Team & Workforce Connect – Maintains strong, regular connect with manpower, contract workforce, and internal teams to understand ground-level concerns, ensure smooth communication, and keep HR processes and site operations streamlined.

Project & Program Management – Contributes to or independently manages assigned HR development projects, programs, and site-level initiatives.

Stakeholder Management – Liaises with external stakeholders (contractors, vendors, local authorities, consultants) to ensure the organization consistently receives agreed standards of service.

title: Consulting Engineer
description:
Meet the Team

Cisco's Customer Experience (CX) Professional Services Service Provider PDI (Plan, Design, Implement) team is a group of elite technical experts driving the architecture, deployment, and optimization of 5G Core, Telco Cloud, and edge computing infrastructures for Japan's leading telecommunications carriers.

We are leading the monumental industry shift from legacy hardware-centric networks toward modern, agile, and resilient Telco Cloud platforms powered by Kubernetes and advanced virtualization. Working in close synergy with Cisco's global Business Units (BU) and Centers of Excellence (CoE), we operate as One Team to architect and deploy mission-critical mobile platforms that demand world-class reliability, ultra-low latency, and massive throughput.

Your Impact

As a Consulting Engineer, you will act as a technical lead responsible for the end-to-end design, implementation, and performance optimization of Kubernetes/KVM-based cloud-native infrastructures and high-speed data planes leveraging CNDP (Cloud Native Data Plane) for Japan's tier-1 Service Provider clients.

You will own the complete technical delivery lifecycle-from customer requirement scoping and Detailed Design (LLD) authoring to configuration manifest creation, PoC/lab staging, field implementation, kernel/data-plane tuning, and production cutover-ensuring a robust, high-performance foundation for 5G Cloud-native Network Functions (CNFs) and Virtual Network Functions (VNFs).

What You'll Do

• Cloud-Native Architecture & Design: Lead the High-Level and Low-Level Design (HLD/LLD), parameter definition, and test plan creation for bare-metal / VM-based Kubernetes and KVM/OpenStack virtualization platforms in 5G Core and edge environments.

• Data Plane Acceleration & Performance Tuning: Apply high-speed packet processing technologies-including CNDP (Cloud Native Data Plane), DPDK, SR-IOV, and eBPF-to conduct benchmarking, kernel parameter tuning, and throughput optimization meeting stringent carrier-grade SLAs.

• Container Network Interface (CNI) Engineering: Architect, integrate, and troubleshoot advanced container networking environments utilizing Multus CNI, Calico, SR-IOV CNI, and high-performance routing protocols.

• PDI Technical Delivery & Cutover Ownership: Serve as the technical lead across the full PDI lifecycle, driving staging validation, on-site deployment, cutover runbook execution, and real-time risk mitigation during critical maintenance windows.

• Global Collaboration & Knowledge Scaling: Partner with global architecture teams (India CoE, US BU Engineering) to resolve complex product roadblocks, while translating project learnings into reusable templates and design collateral for the broader team.

Who You Are

You are a seasoned infrastructure and platform engineer with deep Linux/Kubernetes expertise, a strong data-plane engineering mindset, and proven execution discipline in large-scale Service Provider environments.

Minimum Qualifications:

• 5+ years of hands-on experience in the design, deployment, and operation of container platforms (Kubernetes / Docker) or enterprise virtualization environments (KVM / OpenStack).

• Deep understanding of Linux OS internals (RHEL / Ubuntu), kernel parameter tuning, system administration, and container network stack troubleshooting.

• Practical knowledge or implementation experience with accelerated data-plane technologies (e.g., CNDP, DPDK, SR-IOV, eBPF, or fast packet processing).

• End-to-end PDI (Plan, Design, Implement) delivery capability, including authoring Detailed Design documents (LLD), execution runbooks, and test verification procedures.

• Native or business-level fluency in Japanese (client-facing advisory and technical documentation) with professional working proficiency in English (collaborating with global engineering teams).

Preferred Qualifications:

• Practical experience deploying or validating 5G Core components (UPF, SMF), vEPC, or Telco CNFs (Cloud-native Network Functions).

• Professional certifications such as CKA (Certified Kubernetes Administrator), CKAD, RHCA, or RHCE.

• Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and automation experience utilizing Python, Bash, Ansible, Terraform, or GitOps frameworks.

• Familiarity with CI/CD delivery pipelines (GitLab, Jenkins) and containerized deployment workflows.

• Understanding of Cisco compute/networking solutions (Cisco UCS servers, Nexus switches, Cisco Telco Cloud architecture).

Why Cisco?

At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.

Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.

We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

Als medewerker spoelkeuken ben jij hierin een belangrijke schakel. Je hoeft geen horeca-ervaring te hebben om bij ons te starten. We zoeken vooral iemand die graag de handen uit de mouwen steekt, afspraken nakomt en het leuk vindt om samen met collega's de klus te klaren.
